exact.c1.1.closed-field-contract.description: The public OIDC and OAuth metadata endpoints return independent documents whose complete non-null P0/P1 key sets exactly match the literal C1.1 shared, OIDC-only, OIDC-required, and phase-gated contract; P0 omits revocation metadata and P1 publishes the same-origin endpoint plus the exact registered-client auth-method set in both documents.

exact.c1.1.cimd-gate.description: Both public metadata documents return HTTP 200 and omit client_id_metadata_document_supported while CIMD is disabled or below P1; at P1 they publish true only for a SaaS tenant with a non-empty tenant policy and keep an unconfigured sibling tenant omitted.

exact.c1.1b.discovery.description: SaaS discovery derives distinct tenant issuers and tenant-local endpoint origins from the request Host while preserving each tenant subject profile; for the same P2 token body, the control-plane Host fails with invalid_request before issuance while a valid tenant Host passes Host routing and reaches registered client authentication as invalid_client.

exact.c2.1.access-token-shape.description: A real authorization-code exchange returns an at+jwt access token whose header is ES256, whose signature verifies independently against the public EC JWKS, and whose namespaced sub_type is user.

exact.c2.2a.access-signer-shape.description: The access-token signer emits the canonical private-claim namespace and keeps an ordinary single-resource token below the 4 KiB soft target.

exact.c2.2a.delegation-signer-shape.description: The delegation-token signer keeps RFC 8693 act pure, emits the canonical private-claim namespace, and keeps an ordinary delegated token below the 4 KiB soft target.

exact.c2.2b.introspection-namespace.description: AS introspection preserves the delegated token signer namespace byte-for-byte, including sub_type, auth_grant, and actor_types, and returns the pure RFC 8693 act object.

exact.c2.3a.2lo-sub.description: Real P2 client_credentials issuance in both public and pairwise subject modes produces agent tokens whose sub and client_id equal the workload client_id and whose sub remains identical across two resource servers.

exact.c2.3.service-2lo.description: A real public token endpoint issues independently verifiable sub_type=service tokens through client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and private_key_jwt. Malformed private-key assertions for a known service, including mixed body-secret and Basic variants, remain registered-client invalid_request failures with service audit attribution; a known workload with a malformed assertion remains on the workload audit path. It rejects wrong credentials, public/workload records, a none-auth confidential record, an ordinary confidential client without an explicit 2LO resource policy, out-of-policy resources/scopes, missing or malformed required DPoP, and a tombstoned service. Under both Public and Pairwise user-subject modes, the service sub equals client_id and remains stable across two resource servers; valid required DPoP is reflected in cnf.jkt.

exact.c2.3.workload-jwt-routing.description: A valid workload OIDC JWT whose unverified iss and sub are equal is still selected by the managed workload trust path rather than being mistaken for a registered service private_key_jwt assertion.

exact.c2.3.service-policy-snapshot.description: Deterministic winning and losing legacy-secret migration CAS cases both reload the ClientStore credential and 2LO policy snapshot, then complete service authorization, sign access tokens, verify their ES256 signatures, and prove the issued audience and scope come only from the exact reloaded snapshots whose credentials authenticated. A third CAS-loss case reloads a concurrent tombstone and proves authentication fails without signing.

exact.c2.2b.python-offline-sdk.description: The Python offline verifier exposes the signer actor_types namespace map.

exact.c2.2b.python-introspection-sdk.description: The Python introspection client exposes the AS actor_types namespace map.

exact.c2.2b.typescript-offline-sdk.description: The TypeScript offline verifier exposes the signer actor_types namespace map.

exact.c2.2b.typescript-introspection-sdk.description: The TypeScript introspection client exposes the AS actor_types namespace map.

exact.c8.2.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK enforces exact single-audience and per-user subject policy, defaults scope implication to exact matching, permits only explicit transitive implications, rejects cyclic SDK configuration, and proves baseline signature, time, issuer, token-shape, client, and audience validation runs before policy resolution.

exact.c8.2.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK enforces exact single-audience and per-user subject policy, defaults scope implication to exact matching, permits only explicit transitive implications, rejects cyclic SDK configuration, and proves baseline signature, time, issuer, token-shape, client, and audience validation runs before policy resolution.

exact.c8.3.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK accepts valid ES256 and RS256 tokens, rejects cryptographically valid signatures whose kid selects the opposite key type, rejects unsupported RSA algorithms for an RSA kid, and rejects alg none.

exact.c8.3.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK accepts valid ES256 and RS256 tokens, rejects cryptographically valid signatures whose kid selects the opposite key type, rejects unsupported RSA algorithms for an RSA kid, and rejects alg none.

exact.c8.4.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK refetches JWKS for rotated unknown kids, resumes after rate-limit and negative-cache expiry, isolates negative entries per kid, single-flights concurrent misses, and preserves old keys on fetch failure.

exact.c8.4.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK refetches JWKS for rotated unknown kids, resumes after rate-limit and negative-cache expiry, isolates negative entries per kid, single-flights concurrent misses, and preserves old keys on fetch failure.

exact.c8.5a.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK exposes the v1 built-in vocabulary and enforces RFC3339 and epoch time, exact and slash-prefix resources, record-count, locations, malformed and unknown constraints, per-detail AND, and cross-detail OR boundaries.

exact.c8.5a.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK exposes the v1 built-in vocabulary and enforces RFC3339 and epoch time, exact and slash-prefix resources, record-count, locations, malformed and unknown constraints, per-detail AND, and cross-detail OR boundaries.

exact.c8.5b.python-policy-boundary.description: The Python evaluator dispatch is deny-only and fail-closed, runs SDK-owned v1 constraints before extension evaluation, passes frozen defensive copies of detail and request plus an immutable primitive claims projection, and proves the public low-level RAR helper cannot accept an evaluator bypass.

exact.c8.5b.python-offline-binding.description: The Python offline SDK invokes complex RAR only after signature, exact single audience, sub_type, and route scope validation, rejects top-level and per-detail malformed authorization_details before evaluator invocation, and maps evaluator denial to a token-free 403.

exact.c8.5b.python-introspection-binding.description: The Python introspection authorization seam invokes complex RAR only after strict boolean active, exact single audience, sub_type, and route scope validation, rejects top-level and per-detail malformed authorization_details before evaluator invocation, and fails closed on evaluator denial.

exact.c8.5b.typescript-policy-boundary.description: The TypeScript evaluator dispatch is deny-only and fail-closed, runs SDK-owned v1 constraints before extension evaluation, passes frozen defensive copies of detail and request plus an immutable primitive claims projection, and proves the public low-level RAR helper ignores a dynamically injected evaluator bypass.

exact.c8.5b.typescript-offline-binding.description: The TypeScript offline SDK invokes complex RAR only after signature, exact single audience, sub_type, and route scope validation, rejects top-level and per-detail malformed authorization_details before evaluator invocation, and maps evaluator denial to a token-free 403.

exact.c8.5b.typescript-introspection-bin.description: The TypeScript introspection authorization seam invokes complex RAR only after strict boolean active, exact single audience, sub_type, and route scope validation, rejects top-level and per-detail malformed authorization_details before evaluator invocation, and fails closed on evaluator denial.

exact.c8.6.aud-and-namespace.description: An authenticated, enabled RS can introspect audiences at the first, middle, and last positions of its registered resource set and receives the non-delegated namespace, while another RS receives only active:false and no token fields.

exact.c8.6.inactive-indistinguishability.description: Invalid tokens and valid tokens outside the caller's registered resource set produce the same field-minimal active:false response.

exact.c8.6.auth-and-permission.description: Anonymous, unknown, wrong-secret, and non-introspection clients are rejected before token state is exposed.

exact.c8.6.none-auth-rejected.description: An inconsistent client marked introspection-enabled but configured with the none authentication method is rejected fail closed.

exact.c8.7a.rar-reflection.description: A P2 code-flow token carrying admitted, resource-bound RAR is introspected with authorization_details exactly equal to the signed access-token claim.

exact.c8.7b.authorization-code.description: A real authorization-code exchange with a valid DPoP proof returns an ES256 at+jwt access token whose cnf.jkt equals the proof key thumbprint and token_type is DPoP.

exact.c8.7b.authorization-code-bearer.description: A real authorization-code exchange without a DPoP proof returns token_type Bearer and an access token without an invented cnf.

exact.c7b.1.exactly-one-hint.description: POST /bc-authorize rejects a missing user hint, every pair of login_hint, login_hint_token, and id_token_hint, and all three hints together as invalid_request.

exact.c7b.1.id-token-resolution.description: A valid signed id_token_hint and login_hint resolve to the same active user through POST /bc-authorize and therefore share the same per-user cooldown boundary.

exact.c7b.1.id-token-tamper.description: POST /bc-authorize rejects a tampered id_token_hint signature as invalid_request instead of accepting or downgrading the hint.

exact.c7b.1.id-token-audience.description: POST /bc-authorize rejects an otherwise signed id_token_hint whose audience does not identify the requesting client.

exact.c7b.1.login-hint-token-fail-closed.description: The currently unsupported login_hint_token form is rejected fail closed as invalid_request and is not silently treated as another hint type.

exact.c7b.2.poll-errors.description: A real CIBA authorization request is polled through POST /token and returns authorization_pending, slow_down while the authoritative last poll remains inside the advertised interval, authorization_pending again outside that interval, and expired_token after the request expires.

exact.c7b.poll-interval-boundary.description: The shared CIBA/device polling decision returns slow_down through the final second inside the advertised interval and resumes the persistent pending state exactly at the interval boundary.

exact.c7b.poll-claim-memory.description: The in-memory CIBA and device stores compare-and-set the observed last_poll_at under one lock, so two concurrent claims for one interval slot have exactly one winner.

exact.c7b.poll-claim-dynamo.description: The production DynamoDB CIBA and device stores condition last_poll_at updates on the exact observed value, use attribute_not_exists for the first poll, and report a conditional-write conflict as a lost interval claim; device claims additionally require expires_at > :now in the same condition.

exact.c7b.2.concurrent-pending.description: Two concurrent public CIBA POST /token polls for one pending request produce exactly one authorization_pending response and one slow_down response.

exact.c7b.4.concurrent-pending.description: Two concurrent public device-code POST /token polls for one pending grant produce exactly one authorization_pending response and one slow_down response.

exact.c7b.2.denied.description: A denied CIBA authorization request is polled through POST /token and returns the standard access_denied error.

exact.c7b.2.approved-one-shot.description: An unknown CIBA auth_req_id fails without recording client activity; an approved request returns a user access token from POST /token, advances the client's last_used_day, and a serial replay of the consumed auth_req_id returns invalid_grant.

exact.c7b.3.sessionless-poll.description: The cross-user approver and represented user both log out through the public endpoint and prove their old cookies no longer resolve server-side sessions; after the represented user has approved, a standard CIBA client still obtains the user access token from POST /token using only grant_type, auth_req_id, and client_id, without a browser cookie, Authorization header, session token, or /sessions request.

exact.c7b.6.user-cooldown.description: POST /bc-authorize accepts the first request for one registered user, rejects an immediate repeat and a case-variant of the same email as 429 temporarily_unavailable, and still accepts a different registered user.

exact.c7b.6.approval-display.description: The authenticated approval-details endpoint always returns the requesting client, preserves a supplied binding_message byte-for-byte, returns null when it was absent, and leaves the request authorization_pending after the details are viewed.

exact.c7b.6.approval-page.description: The browser approval page renders the requesting client and a supplied binding_message verbatim, omits the verification-message region when the field is absent, and sends no approval decision merely by displaying either request.

exact.c7b.5.registration.description: A P3 deployment with the capability enabled accepts a confidential ping client with an HTTPS notification endpoint through the public dynamic-registration endpoint.

exact.c7b.5.confidential-only.description: Dynamic registration rejects ping delivery for a public client instead of creating a callback credential that cannot authenticate at the token endpoint.

exact.c7b.5.endpoint-ssrf.description: Dynamic registration rejects non-HTTPS, metadata, private-address, non-443, and userinfo-confused notification endpoints before a ping or push callback can be configured.

exact.c7b.5.endpoint-required.description: A ping registration without a backchannel notification endpoint fails closed with invalid_client_metadata.

exact.c7b.5.capability-gate.description: Ping registration is rejected both before P3 and when the P3 capability flag is disabled, so unsupported delivery modes cannot be stored or advertised as usable.

exact.c7b.5.poll-compatibility.description: Enabling ping and push preserves explicit and default poll registration for public clients.

exact.c7b.5.ping-dispatch.description: Approval dispatches exactly one ping callback containing the auth_req_id and bound client_notification_token, leaves the request unconsumed, and permits the confidential client to obtain the access token through POST /token.

exact.c7b.5.poll-auth.description: An approved ping request cannot be redeemed with auth_req_id alone: the confidential client must authenticate at POST /token.

exact.c7b.5.snapshot.description: Callback dispatch uses the notification endpoint snapshotted when the CIBA request was created rather than a later-mutated client record.

exact.c7b.5.downgrade-rejection.description: Downgrading a ping or push client to token_endpoint_auth_method none after request creation does not turn the stored delivery-mode snapshot into an unauthenticated token redemption path.

exact.c7b.5.discovery.description: OIDC discovery advertises poll, ping, and push only at P3 with the capability enabled and otherwise advertises poll alone.

exact.c7b.6.global-push-quota.description: An unexhausted shared CIBA callback quota permits a push delivery containing an access token; after the same quota is deterministically exhausted, approving ping and push requests creates no additional callback delivery while both clients can still obtain their approved tokens through authenticated poll fallback.

exact.c7b.2.concurrent-one-shot.description: Two concurrent POST /token polls for one approved CIBA request produce exactly one successful token response.

exact.c7b.4.poll-errors.description: A real device authorization publishes a positive code lifetime no greater than 15 minutes that matches the authoritative expiry, then POST /token returns authorization_pending, slow_down inside the advertised interval, authorization_pending outside it, and expired_token after the grant expires.

exact.c7b.4.denied.description: A denied device authorization is polled through POST /token and returns the standard access_denied error.

exact.c7b.4.one-shot.description: An unknown device code fails without recording client activity; an approved device code issues one access token, advances the client's last_used_day, and a second POST /token with the same consumed code is rejected as invalid_grant.

exact.c7b.4.concurrent-one-shot.description: Two concurrent POST /token polls for one approved device code produce exactly one successful token response, and later replay remains invalid_grant.

exact.c8.7b.refresh.description: A DPoP-bound refresh family rejects missing or different-key proofs and rotates only with the matching proof, returning an ES256 at+jwt access token while preserving token_type DPoP and the same cnf.jkt.

exact.c8.7b.workload.description: Real workload client-credentials exchanges return ES256 at+jwt access tokens: DPoP with the exact proof-key JKT when a proof is present and Bearer without an invented cnf when it is absent.

exact.c8.7b.device.description: Approved device-code polls return ES256 at+jwt access tokens: DPoP with the exact proof-key JKT when a proof is present and Bearer without an invented cnf when it is absent.

exact.c8.7b.ciba.description: Approved CIBA polls return ES256 at+jwt access tokens: DPoP with the exact proof-key JKT when a proof is present and Bearer without an invented cnf when it is absent.

exact.c8.7b.ema.description: EMA independently verifies every successful access-token signature and fixes its header to ES256 at+jwt while binding a proof key, preserving a matching assertion cnf, or returning Bearer without cnf when proof-free; a malformed proof fails without token fields or Bearer downgrade.

exact.c13.1.feature-off.description: With EMA disabled by default, both live metadata documents omit the ID-JAG profile and JWT bearer grant, while a JWT bearer token request returns no-store unsupported_grant_type.

exact.c13.1.feature-on-no-probe.description: A complete P2 EMA state makes both live metadata documents announce the exact ID-JAG profile and JWT bearer grant, while observable cached and fresh JWKS fetch counters remain zero.

exact.c13.1.dependency-gate.description: Both live metadata documents omit the profile and grant when policy, replay, JTI mapping, P2 phase, or SaaS tenant partitioning is absent.

exact.c13.1.metadata-golden.description: Complete serialized P2 OIDC and OAuth metadata remain byte-for-byte equal to their pre-EMA golden documents when the feature is off.

exact.c13.1.deployment-config.description: CDK injects the EMA flag, secret-backed policy, JTI table, P2 phase, and deployment provenance into both runtimes only for a complete enabled deployment, and synth fails closed for missing, malformed, oversized, premature, or unbound configuration.

exact.c13.3.policy-index.description: A validated EMA policy preserves the exact trusted issuer, optional issuer tenant, HTTPS JWKS URI, RS256 and ES256 allowlist, authenticated-to-assertion client mapping, and resource scope set.

exact.c13.3.policy-validation.description: EMA startup policy validation rejects insecure issuer or JWKS schemes, unsafe JWKS hosts, invalid issuer tenants or client mappings, empty or duplicate algorithm sets, and empty, duplicate, or ambiguous resource and scope configuration.

exact.c13.3.identity-time-decision.description: The bounded authorization decision enforces exact issuer and issuer-tenant matching, including the optional-tenant absence rule, exact assertion client and audience, policy-pinned algorithm, required subject, and assertion time bounds.

exact.c13.3.http-claim-signature.description: The live JWT bearer endpoint rejects missing or mismatched issuer, issuer tenant, audience, and assertion client; missing subject, exp, iat, jti, or scope; and mismatched resource. Wrong typ, time, signature, and policy-pinned algorithm also fail without an access token or unrelated key refresh.

exact.c13.3.http-key-selection.description: A no-kid ES256 assertion succeeds when a multi-key JWKS has exactly one algorithm-compatible key, while duplicate matching kid entries fail as ambiguous without a refresh fallback.

exact.c13.3.http-rs256.description: A real 2048-bit RS256 ID-JAG is verified through the public JWT bearer token endpoint with the policy-fixed JWKS and produces an access token.

exact.c13.3.fixed-trust-anchor.description: Attacker-controlled jku, x5u, and jwks_uri values cannot select a signing key: the endpoint reads only the policy-fixed JWKS URI, never reads or refreshes the attacker URI, and rejects the attacker-signed assertion.

exact.c13.4.resource-scope-decision.description: The pure EMA decision accepts an exact resource string or containing URI array but emits only the requested resource and scope subset; it rejects malformed or unknown request targets, missing strict-mode resources, empty, duplicate, invalid, or non-containing assertion resources, invalid scope syntax, and assertion or policy scope expansion. Legacy missing-resource compatibility succeeds only for an explicitly enabled single target and multi-target configuration is rejected as ambiguous.

exact.c13.4.rar-actor-dpop-decision.description: The pure EMA decision maps request RAR to invalid_authorization_details; accepts absent or empty assertion RAR; rejects malformed or well-formed nonempty RAR and any act claim; validates cnf as one bounded nonempty jkt; rejects missing or mismatched proof binding; and preserves a matching assertion or request proof without inventing cnf when both are absent.

exact.c13.4.http-scope.description: The public JWT bearer endpoint rejects empty or duplicate requested scope, scope beyond the assertion, and scope beyond policy with invalid_scope, without JIT creation or replay consumption; the same assertion then succeeds for its allowed scope.

exact.c13.4.http-target-rar.description: The public JWT bearer endpoint maps missing, malformed, or unregistered request resource to invalid_target and direct request authorization_details to invalid_authorization_details; none consumes the assertion, which succeeds afterward.

exact.c13.4.http-strict-resource.description: With the public EMA policy in strict mode, an assertion missing resource returns token-free invalid_grant; a corrected assertion with the same jti then succeeds, proving the strict failure did not consume replay state.

exact.c13.4.http-assertion-semantics.description: The public JWT bearer endpoint returns token-free invalid_grant for malformed or well-formed nonempty assertion RAR, act, assertion cnf without proof, and assertion cnf with a valid but mismatched DPoP proof.

exact.c13.5.replay-expiry.description: The bounded EMA authorization decision carries the assertion jti and sets the replay expiration to the assertion exp plus the configured clock skew.

exact.c13.5.partition-derivation.description: Replay and enterprise-user keys are domain separated; the stable enterprise-user key changes independently with Agent Auth tenant, trusted issuer, present or absent issuer tenant, and subject.

exact.c13.6.http-controlled-jit.description: A valid public EMA request creates the derived canonical enterprise user as Active with empty email, no local or SCIM identity binding, and maps the issued access-token jti back to that stable user id.

exact.c13.6.http-email-no-link.description: Two assertions for the same stable subject but different email claims map to the same empty-email enterprise user; an existing local owner of one email remains distinct and unchanged.

exact.c13.6.http-lifecycle-rereads.description: An Active canonical user changing to Disabled after the pre-consume read or Tombstoned after the post-consume read is rejected by the next issuance reread with no token response, while the replay fence remains consumed.

exact.c13.7.http-access-contract.description: For public and pairwise subject profiles, the EMA endpoint returns exactly one Bearer access-token contract with resource, narrowed scope, and a 900-second expiry and no refresh or ID token; an independent EC verifier proves ES256 at+jwt, one audience, authenticated client, user namespace, stable public or resource-sector pairwise subject, and a JTI mapping whose expiry equals the signed exp.

exact.c13.5.http-serial-replay.description: The public EMA endpoint issues once for an assertion and rejects its serial replay with token-free invalid_grant.

exact.c13.5.http-lifecycle-preconsume.description: A disabled enterprise user is rejected before replay consumption; reactivating the same canonical user lets the identical assertion succeed.

exact.c13.5.http-identity-preconsume.description: Active canonical identity conflicts and tombstones are rejected without consuming replay state; the same assertion succeeds after replacing only the user directory with a clean canonical authority.

exact.c13.5.http-preconsumed-no-jit.description: A valid but already-consumed assertion is rejected before enterprise-user JIT, leaving the canonical user absent and returning no token.

exact.c13.5.http-post-jit-reread.description: An injected canonical-user read failure after JIT suppresses issuance, while the created user and consumed assertion prove the replay then JIT then identity-reread order.

exact.c13.5.http-concurrent-replay.description: Two concurrent public EMA requests for one assertion produce exactly one token response and one invalid_grant replay rejection.

exact.c13.5.http-tenant-partition.description: The same upstream jti and subject succeed independently in two Agent Auth tenants, produce distinct tenant-scoped enterprise identities, and issue independently verified access tokens whose issuer matches the request tenant host and whose pairwise subject derives from that tenant's stable user id and the approved resource.

exact.c13.5.http-unknown-kid-refresh.description: An unknown kid triggers exactly one forced refresh after one ordinary read of the policy-fixed JWKS URI, never reads or refreshes an unrelated URI, and then verifies successfully.

exact.c13.5.dynamo-replay.description: The production Dynamo replay adapter writes the tenant-prefixed replay key and exact expiration under one conditional put that accepts only a missing or already-expired row.

exact.c13.5.dynamo-user-read.description: The production canonical-user lookup used by issuance gates sends an exact tenant and user primary key with Dynamo ConsistentRead enabled.

exact.c13.5.jwks-limits.description: The production JWKS parser rejects response bodies over the byte limit and documents over the key-count limit.

exact.c13.5.jwks-force-singleflight.description: Sixteen concurrent forced JWKS refreshes for one URI share exactly one network attempt and one failure result.

exact.c13.5.jwks-force-cooldown.description: A failed forced refresh preserves a still-valid cached key, records failure completion, and rate-limits the next forced refresh without another network attempt.

exact.c13.5.jwks-force-after-cache.description: A recent ordinary JWKS cache fill does not suppress the one forced network attempt required for an unknown kid.

exact.c13.5.jwks-negative-cache.description: Concurrent cold JWKS reads single-flight one network failure and a later read reuses the negative cache without another attempt.

exact.c13.2.ema-request-boundary.description: The EMA JWT bearer grant independently authenticates a registered confidential client, rejects missing, wrong, public, and cross-client credentials, rejects ID-JAG placement in client_assertion or RFC 8693 subject/actor token slots, and leaves the assertion usable only through its dedicated assertion slot.

exact.c8.7b.introspection-reflection.description: A live DPoP delegated exchange returns an ES256 at+jwt token whose signed cnf.jkt equals the actor proof key thumbprint, then an authenticated RS introspection receives that exact observed cnf value.

exact.c8.8.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK emits exact discovery and malformed-or-expired invalid-token challenges, redacts validation details, derives RFC 9728 endpoint-path metadata URLs, preserves safe explicit HTTPS overrides, and rejects unsafe resource or metadata URLs.

exact.c8.8.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK emits exact discovery and malformed-or-expired invalid-token challenges, redacts validation details, derives RFC 9728 endpoint-path metadata URLs, preserves safe explicit HTTPS overrides, and rejects unsafe resource or metadata URLs.

exact.c8.8a.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK emits one exact Bearer challenge with the complete operation scope set for missing-token and insufficient-scope paths and rejects scope auth-param injection on both 401 and 403 paths.

exact.c8.8a.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK emits one exact Bearer challenge with the complete operation scope set for missing-token and insufficient-scope paths and rejects scope auth-param injection on both 401 and 403 paths.

exact.c8.8.mcp-interop.description: The official MCP TypeScript SDK 1.30 fixture follows path-derived PRM discovery from a 401, requests the full operation scope set, performs a 403 step-up, and preserves wrong-audience rejection.

exact.c8.9.python-sdk.description: The Python RS SDK accepts a valid proof bound to the token, normalized request URL, method, access-token hash, and nonce, while rejecting signature tampering, JKT mismatch, missing or wrong HTU and HTM, missing, stale, or future IAT, missing or wrong ATH and nonce, and every standard embedded private JWK field.

exact.c8.9.typescript-sdk.description: The TypeScript RS SDK accepts a valid proof bound to the token, normalized request URL, method, access-token hash, and nonce, while rejecting signature tampering, JKT mismatch, missing or wrong HTU and HTM, missing, stale, or future IAT, missing or wrong ATH and nonce, and every standard embedded private JWK field.

exact.c8.10.size-thresholds.description: The shared token budget classifies values below 4 KiB, from 4 KiB through 7 KiB, and above 7 KiB at the exact boundaries.

exact.c8.10.access-oversize.description: The access-token signing helper rejects a JWT above the hard limit with the distinct TooLarge outcome before producing a signature.

exact.c8.10.delegation-oversize.description: The delegation-token signing helper rejects a JWT above the hard limit with the distinct TooLarge outcome before producing a signature.

exact.c8.10.public-guidance.description: A real POST /token client-credentials request that would produce a JWT above 7 KiB is rejected without a token and returns ASCII guidance to narrow the authorization or use token introspection.

exact.c8.10b.rust-code-refresh.description: A real P3 authorization-code and refresh lifecycle signs verifiable access tokens below 4 KiB with one bounded Grant summary and authenticated introspection returns the complete ordered RAR. Digest drift makes the old token inactive; marked families fail closed for revoked, expired, unreadable, wrong-resource, or missing Grants before refresh rotation, proven by restoring authority and successfully reusing the same refresh token after each failure. Large-summary Grant persistence failure returns no access, refresh, ID, or token-type value, while an inline small-RAR fallback omits the unusable refresh credential.

exact.c8.10b.rust-token-exchange.description: A real P3 token exchange signs a verifiable delegated token below 4 KiB with one bounded Grant summary, while the target RS obtains the complete ordered source-Grant RAR through authenticated introspection.

exact.c8.10b.python-offline-fail-closed.description: The Python offline RS SDK rejects a correctly signed, audience- and scope-valid Grant summary with insufficient_scope and directs the caller to authenticated introspection instead of treating the summary as absent RAR.

exact.c8.10b.typescript-offline-fail-clo.description: The TypeScript offline RS SDK rejects a correctly signed, audience- and scope-valid Grant summary with insufficient_scope and directs the caller to authenticated introspection instead of treating the summary as absent RAR.

exact.c8.10b.delivery-gating.description: Grant-backed delivery is explicit opt-in: small P3 RAR stays inline, the same below-hard-limit large RAR stays inline when the profile is disabled, and only the enabled P3 path replaces it with a bounded summary.

exact.c8.10b.summary-parser.description: The Grant-summary parser accepts only the single fixed v1 shape, canonicalizes object-key order while preserving array order, and rejects mixed details, extra fields, disabled introspection, multiple resources, non-array input, wrong digest width, and independent resource/count/digest/order mismatches.

exact.c2.4.production_nesting.description: Token exchange and subsequent introspection preserve a three-hop nested RFC 8693 act chain and its complete actor_types namespace.

exact.c2.5a.encoder.description: The shared access-token audience encoder always emits one string in a JSON array.

exact.c2.5a.reject-bare.description: The shared token-shape validator rejects a bare-string audience.

exact.c2.5a.reject-multi.description: The shared token-shape validator rejects a multi-element audience array.

exact.c2.5a.reject-empty.description: The shared token-shape validator rejects an empty audience array.

exact.c2.5a.p0-resource-gate.description: A P0 authorization request accepts one resource and rejects both two and three resources, while the P1 controls accept the same multi-resource requests.

exact.c2.6-c2.9.id-token-boundary.description: A real code flow with the default RS256 ID-token algorithm still returns an ES256 at+jwt access token, preventing the per-client ID-token choice from leaking into access-token signing.

exact.c2.7.es256-client.description: DCR persists an explicit ES256 ID-token algorithm; the real code flow returns ES256 ID and access tokens that independently verify against the public JWKS.

exact.c2.10.claim-omission.description: A resource outside the workload client's policy is rejected without recording activity; a valid client_credentials exchange advances last_used_day and returns a 2LO token that omits user-only auth_time, Grant, and delegation claims.

exact.c2.10.strict-claim-omission.description: A real client-credentials token omits Grant, actor-chain, and user-authentication claims from both the JWT top level and the private namespace, and unfiltered physical record counts prove issuance persists no Grant.

exact.c4.1.pkce-method.description: The shared PKCE validator rejects both plain and omitted challenge methods whenever a challenge is supplied.

exact.c4.1.rfc7636-vector.description: The S256 implementation matches the RFC 7636 Appendix B verifier and challenge vector.

exact.c4.1.verifier-format.description: The shared verifier validator enforces the RFC 7636 length bounds and unreserved character set.

exact.c4.1.authorize-public-required.description: The authorization endpoint rejects a public authorization-code request that omits PKCE.

exact.c4.1.authorize-confidential-tuple.description: A registered confidential client receives the PKCE exemption only for a completely omitted tuple, never for method-only or empty-challenge input.

exact.c4.1.authorize-runtime-capability.description: A registered private_key_jwt client cannot omit PKCE when the runtime dependency required to execute that authentication method is disabled.

exact.c4.1.confidential-basic.description: A registered client_secret_basic confidential client completes authorization and token exchange without PKCE only after successful client authentication.

exact.c4.1.confidential-basic-auth.description: Wrong Basic credentials reject a PKCE-less confidential code without consuming it, and the same code succeeds after correct authentication.

exact.c4.1.confidential-post.description: A registered client_secret_post confidential client completes a full authorization-code flow without PKCE.

exact.c4.1.confidential-private-key-jwt.description: A DCR-created private_key_jwt confidential client completes a full authorization-code flow without PKCE using a valid endpoint-bound assertion.

exact.c4.1.token-client-downgrade.description: The token endpoint rechecks current client eligibility, rejects a PKCE-less code after confidential-to-public downgrade, and releases the code for a restored eligible record.

exact.c4.1.token-workload-reclassificati.description: The token endpoint rejects an authorization code after its client becomes workload, before authentication consumes the code, and succeeds after the eligible type is restored.

exact.c4.1.token-unexpected-verifier.description: The token endpoint returns invalid_request when a code authorized without a challenge is exchanged with either an empty or non-empty verifier.

exact.c4.1.token-challenge-binding.description: A confidential client that sent an S256 challenge cannot use its authentication exemption to omit or mismatch the verifier at token exchange.

exact.c4.1.cimd-required.description: A confidential CIMD snapshot cannot receive the ClientStore-only PKCE exemption.

exact.c4.1.consent-public.description: Direct consent continuation cannot bypass the public-client PKCE requirement.

exact.c4.1.consent-confidential.description: Consent continuation allows a registered confidential client with an executable non-none authentication method to omit PKCE.

exact.c4.1.consent-tuple.description: Consent continuation rejects method-only and empty-challenge tuples instead of granting the confidential exemption.

exact.c4.1.consent-workload.description: Direct consent continuation cannot issue an authorization code to a workload client.

exact.c4.1.par-public.description: PAR rejects a public authorization-code request that omits PKCE.

exact.c4.1.par-confidential.description: PAR allows a registered confidential client with successful client_secret_post authentication to omit PKCE.

exact.c4.1.par-tuple.description: PAR rejects method-only and empty-challenge tuples instead of granting the confidential exemption.

exact.c4.1.par-workload.description: PAR refuses to create an authorization-code request for a workload client even when PKCE and client authentication are present.

exact.c4.2.registry-metadata.description: OIDC and OAuth metadata advertise exactly the executable registered-client authentication methods for token and revocation.

exact.c4.2.phase-projection.description: Phase-gated workload methods appear only in token metadata while revocation remains limited to the registered-client registry.

exact.c4.2.admission-registry.description: DCR, Admin, and RFC 7592 admit every executable registered-client method, expose the same registry, and reject invalid private_key_jwt key-source configurations.

exact.c4.2.invalid-record-fail-closed.description: Legacy private_key_jwt records with missing key metadata remain repairable through management APIs but cannot authenticate at runtime.

exact.c4.2.token-auth-matrix.description: Each advertised token authentication method has a real successful exchange and an invalid-credential rejection with an auditable invalid_client result.

exact.c4.2.revocation-auth-matrix.description: Each advertised revocation authentication method succeeds with valid credentials and rejects invalid credentials.

exact.c4.2.method-substitution.description: Token and revocation reject all twelve directed substitutions among none, basic, post, and private_key_jwt with 401 invalid_client.

exact.c4.2.general-inline-jwks.description: OIDF-shaped DCR accepts general inline RS256 JWK metadata without kid for a basic-auth client and preserves the omission.

exact.c4.2.private-inline-kid.description: The same inline key shape is rejected as invalid_client_metadata when private_key_jwt requires a unique non-empty kid.

exact.c4.2.general-key-replacement.description: General jwks_uri metadata survives an omitted Admin PATCH and is cleared by full-replacement PUT when omitted.

exact.c4.2.private-claims-replay.description: Private-key JWT authentication rejects wrong audience, issuer or subject, expiry, unknown key, algorithm confusion, and jti replay.

exact.c4.2.private-jwks-uri.description: Token authentication loads and verifies an ES256 private-key assertion from the client's registered remote JWKS URI.

exact.c4.2.private-rs256.description: A client pinned to RS256 completes token authentication with its registered inline RSA public key.

exact.c4.2.private-key-rotation.description: Inline key rotation accepts both keys during overlap and rejects the removed key immediately after the registered set changes.

exact.c4.2.private-replay-dependency.description: Without the replay authority, discovery and admission stop advertising private_key_jwt and persisted clients fail closed.

exact.c4.2.private-revocation.description: Revocation accepts a private-key assertion bound to the exact revocation endpoint audience.

exact.c4.2.private-introspection.description: Introspection authenticates an enabled client with a private-key assertion bound to the introspection endpoint.

exact.c4.2.private-par.description: PAR accepts a private-key assertion bound to the pushed-authorization endpoint.

exact.c4.2.private-refresh.description: Refresh rotation requires and accepts a fresh private-key assertion at the token endpoint.

exact.c4.2.private-ciba.description: CIBA ping authenticates private-key JWT separately at backchannel authorization and token issuance with endpoint-specific audiences.

exact.c4.2.private-prm.description: The PRM POST endpoint authenticates a body-carried private-key assertion without exposing it in the URL.

exact.c4.2.private-sessions.description: Session list and detail POST endpoints require body-carried private-key assertions with exact per-route audiences.

exact.c4.2.general-key-migration.description: Changing away from private_key_jwt clears its signing-algorithm pin while preserving the JWK set as general client metadata.

exact.c4.3.registration-uri.description: Open DCR returns a server-generated registration_client_uri exactly equal to the trusted issuer origin plus /register/{client_id}, and the issued client completes a real authorization-code flow.

exact.c4.3.untrusted-host.description: A DCR request with an untrusted Host is rejected as invalid_client_metadata before any dynamic client is persisted.

exact.c4.3.management-ownership.description: RFC 7592 management accepts only the matching registration token; missing, forged, cross-client, and admin-domain tokens are rejected, PATCH returns no replacement token while preserving the original, and DELETE invalidates it.

exact.c4.3.anonymous-ip-throttle.description: Anonymous open DCR registrations from source A receive 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After after its per-IP burst bucket is exhausted while source B remains admitted and source A remains throttled.

exact.c4.3.iat-routing.description: After t1 anonymous open-DCR capacity is exhausted, an explicit invalid IAT is rejected without anonymous fallback; a valid t1 IAT consumes its own one-request quota, cannot authorize t2, and does not consume t2's independent IAT quota.

exact.c4.7.direction-matrix.description: The shared downgrade classifier marks refresh rotation disablement, redirect relaxation, authentication weakening, DPoP relaxation, and token-lifetime extension as downgrades.

exact.c4.7.tightening.description: The shared classifier does not require downgrade confirmation when authentication, redirect matching, or token validity is tightened.

exact.c4.7.unknown-fail-safe.description: Any future managed field that reaches the shared classifier without a defined monotonic direction fails safe as a downgrade.

exact.c4.7.auth-method.description: A public Admin PATCH weakening private_key_jwt to none is rejected without confirmation, preserves the existing record, and succeeds only with explicit confirmation.

exact.c4.7.admin-dpop.description: The Admin API exposes require_dpop and rejects required-to-optional relaxation without confirmation while preserving the public GET state.

exact.c4.7.rfc7592-dpop.description: RFC 7592 PATCH requires confirmation for DPoP relaxation but not tightening; full-replacement PUT omission resets require_dpop to false and is likewise rejected until confirmed.

exact.c4.7.rfc7592-auth-put-default.description: RFC 7592 full-replacement PUT omission resets token_endpoint_auth_method to none, requires downgrade confirmation from a stronger method, and preserves the public GET state when rejected.

exact.c4.7.push-dpop-invariant.description: RFC 7592 updates cannot enable require_dpop for push delivery because that client has no token request on which to present a DPoP proof.

exact.c4.7.immutable-schema.description: The public OpenAPI exposes require_dpop across registration, create, view, PATCH, and PUT contracts while exposing no per-client control that disables mandatory refresh rotation or extends token validity; closed PATCH/PUT property sets force every future mutable field through a C4.7 audit.

exact.c4.8.context-no-logo.description: An open DCR request carrying an impersonating client_name and external logo_uri can create a client, but neither the registration response nor the authenticated consent context reflects those attacker-controlled branding fields.

exact.c4.8.unverified-no-external-logo.description: Even when a registered-client consent response is injected with an external logo_uri, the browser displays the unverified warning, creates no matching image, and sends no request to the attacker-controlled URL.

exact.c4.9.registered-priority.description: A tenant ClientStore record whose client_id is itself a URL completes authorization without making any CIMD request, so remote metadata cannot shadow the control-plane record.

exact.c4.9.url-policy.description: CIMD admission rejects root paths, query or fragment data, userinfo, literal and encoded dot segments, non-default ports, untrusted hosts, and non-HTTPS URLs before fetch.

exact.c4.9.literal-targets.description: CIMD URL validation rejects IPv4 and IPv6 loopback, private, and link-local literal targets even when a hostname policy is otherwise configured.

exact.c4.9.document-contract.description: The document parser requires an exact client_id, non-empty bounded client name and redirect set, valid exact redirect URIs, public metadata without keys, and inline-key private_key_jwt while rejecting shared-secret methods.

exact.c4.9.document-mismatch-http.description: The public authorization endpoint rejects both a fetched document whose client_id differs from its URL and a request redirect absent from the verified document.

exact.c4.9.transport-pinning.description: The production pinned HTTPS client verifies the configured hostname against a controlled TLS server at the resolved address, exposes redirects without following them, rejects oversized bodies, combines cache directives, and enforces the request timeout.

exact.c4.9.redirect-policy.description: A CIMD redirect to a host outside the tenant trust policy is rejected instead of being followed.

exact.c4.9.redirect-limit.description: A redirect chain exceeding the fixed CIMD limit fails closed before an unbounded fetch sequence can continue.

exact.c4.9.dns-address-validation.description: The production pinned HTTPS helper accepts a bounded public DNS answer but rejects mixed public/private, loopback, link-local, IPv6 loopback, and over-limit address sets before building the client.

exact.c4.9.dns-fail-closed.description: The CIMD resolver maps the production transport's unsafe-target result to an invalid client instead of downgrading it to an ordinary network retry.

exact.c4.9.fetch-budget.description: Cold CIMD fetch capacity is bounded per tenant and host: one tenant cannot continue fetching after its budget is exhausted while a sibling tenant retains independent capacity.

exact.c4.9.total-timeout.description: A CIMD dependency that exceeds the resolver's total deadline returns temporarily unavailable instead of waiting without bound.

exact.c4.9.singleflight-timeout.description: A same-URL request waiting behind singleflight receives no fresh timeout window; both the leader and waiter fail within the same bounded resolver deadline.

exact.c4.9.concurrency-bound.description: When the bounded outbound fetch slot is occupied, a different cold URL fails temporarily unavailable without queueing or starting a second network request.

exact.c4.9.cache-store.description: Repeated resolution of one exact URL uses its cached snapshot, while a no-store response is fetched again and never persisted.

exact.c4.9.cache-policy.description: CIMD cache freshness honors Age, s-maxage, no-cache, private, duplicate or malformed directives, and Expires while never exceeding the local maximum TTL.

exact.c4.9.cache-isolation.description: Two exact URLs under one trusted host retain distinct snapshots, the same URL is fetched independently for two tenants, and a tenant without policy cannot read either cache entry.

exact.c4.9.malformed-not-cached.description: A malformed CIMD response fails without entering cache, so a subsequent valid response for the same exact URL is fetched and accepted.

exact.c4.9.oversized-not-cached.description: A CIMD response above the 5 KiB document limit fails without entering cache, so a subsequent bounded response is fetched and accepted.

exact.c4.9.public-snapshot.description: After a public CIMD document changes, authorization-code exchange and refresh both succeed from the authorization-time snapshot and the mutable document is fetched exactly once.

exact.c4.9.private-key-snapshot.description: Code and refresh authentication accept only the inline private_key_jwt key captured at authorization, reject a later document key, perform one CIMD fetch, and redact the URL path from denial events.

exact.c4.9.continuation-binding.description: The continuation MAC accepts only the original session, exact client URL, and CIMD snapshot digest and rejects independent mutation of each bound field.

exact.c4.9.consent-continuation.description: Consent continuation rejects a CIMD document mutation instead of issuing a code from metadata different from the authorization-session digest.

exact.c4.9.login-continuation.description: The authorization continuation after interactive login rejects a changed CIMD snapshot before proceeding to consent or code issuance.

exact.c4.10.normalization.description: The shared registration normalizer defaults omitted application_type to web, accepts native, and rejects unknown request values.

exact.c4.10.web-redirect-matrix.description: The shared redirect validator accepts a public HTTPS DNS host for web clients and rejects HTTP, localhost variants, loopback, private, link-local, and reserved IP literals.

exact.c4.10.native-redirect-matrix.description: The shared redirect validator accepts reverse-domain private-use schemes and HTTP IPv4 or IPv6 loopback for native clients while rejecting remote HTTP, localhost, HTTPS, weak custom schemes, and unrelated URI schemes.

exact.c4.10.native-loopback-match.description: Runtime redirect matching lets a registered native IPv4 loopback callback vary only its ephemeral port, rejects path and IP-family changes, and keeps private-use redirects exact.

exact.c4.10.dcr.description: Public DCR defaults and persists web, accepts native private-use and IPv4 or IPv6 loopback redirects, and rejects invalid web, native, and application_type inputs before persistence.

exact.c4.10.authorize-legacy.description: The authorize endpoint treats both a legacy missing application_type and an unknown persisted value as web and rejects their forbidden localhost redirect.

exact.c4.10.rfc7592.description: RFC 7592 GET, PATCH, and PUT preserve explicit native or web application_type values, and full replacement omission defaults and persists web.

exact.c4.10.admin-legacy.description: Admin views legacy missing and unknown persisted application_type values as web, rejects a forbidden IP-literal redirect update, and normalizes a valid update back to explicit web storage.

exact.c4.10.admin-revalidation.description: Admin application_type changes revalidate the complete redirect set, reject native metadata under the web policy and localhost variants, require downgrade confirmation, and persist the valid web replacement.

exact.c4.10.dynamo.description: DynamoDB round-trips native application_type while missing legacy and unknown persisted values both resolve through the effective web policy.

exact.c4.4a.identical.description: An identical registered and inbound redirect URI is accepted in exact mode.

exact.c4.4a.scheme-case.description: Exact-mode canonicalization compares URI schemes case-insensitively.

exact.c4.4a.host-case.description: Exact-mode canonicalization compares URI hosts case-insensitively.

exact.c4.4a.port.description: Exact mode compares non-loopback ports without treating an explicit default port as omitted.

exact.c4.4a.fuzz.description: Exact mode rejects traversal encodings, double encoding, double and trailing slashes, query changes, userinfo, path-case changes, and fragments.

exact.c4.4a.query.description: A registered raw query is accepted only when the inbound raw query is exactly equal.

exact.c4.4a.no-query.description: Exact mode accepts the no-query case only when both registered and inbound URIs omit a query.

exact.c4.4a.double-encoding.description: Path canonicalization rejects a path that still contains percent encoding after one decode.

exact.c4.4a.encoded-traversal.description: Path canonicalization decodes once and rejects an encoded parent traversal segment.

exact.c4.4a.encoded-delimiters.description: Path canonicalization rejects percent-encoded input that decodes to a double slash, question mark, or fragment delimiter.

exact.c4.4b.canonicalization.description: Inbound prefix matching rejects literal and encoded traversal, encoded delimiters, double encoding, and fragments through the shared path canonicalizer.

exact.c4.4b.registered-canonicalization.description: Registered prefix templates fail closed when percent decoding would synthesize a path separator or wildcard, and for the shared traversal, delimiter, and double-encoding hazards.

exact.c5.1.wrong-oidc-audience.description: A correctly signed upstream workload OIDC assertion with an audience other than this AS returns an explicit invalid-client audience error instead of receiving a 2LO token.

exact.c5.1.platform-and-sts-audiences.description: The OIDC policy rejects assertions targeting either STS or the upstream platform itself instead of this AS.

exact.c5.1.missing-audience.description: The OIDC policy fails closed when the upstream assertion omits its audience claim.

exact.c5.2.sts-signature-rejection.description: A SigV4 JSON assertion reaches the workload STS verifier rather than registered-service JWT parsing, and an invalid AWS signature is returned as invalid_client without issuing a token.

exact.c5.4.sts-timeout.description: The production HttpStsCaller::new path maps a deliberately slow local HTTP dependency to a transient error after its literal two-second request deadline.

exact.c5.4.circuit-breaker.description: Five transient STS failures through POST /token make exactly five STS calls; the sixth request returns 503 without another STS call or any token, while an OIDC client-credentials request against the same open-circuit state still succeeds without touching STS.

exact.c5.4.half-open-boundary.description: The circuit rejects at 29 seconds, allows one half-open probe at the literal 30-second cooldown boundary, and records that probe as in flight.

exact.c5.4.half-open-success.description: A successful half-open probe closes the circuit and permits the next request.

exact.c5.4.half-open-failure.description: A failed half-open probe reopens the circuit with a fresh cooldown and rejects within that new window.

exact.c5.4.half-open-single-probe.description: While the half-open probe is in flight, a concurrent second request is rejected immediately.

exact.c5.6.token-exchange.description: A real token exchange returns an ES256 at+jwt delegated access token with the authorized audience, scope, subject, actor, and source-Grant binding.

exact.c5.7.admin-jwt-binding.description: The authenticated Admin API rejects whole-domain patterns, cross-domain patterns, and reuse of this authorization server's JWKS before registering and returning a tenant-scoped SPIFFE JWT trust binding.

exact.c5.7.admin-x509-binding.description: The authenticated Admin API registers and returns the distinct SPIFFE X.509 trust mechanism without accepting a JWT bundle URI.

exact.c5.7.jwt-es256.description: A valid ES256 JWT-SVID signed by the configured trust bundle completes the public client-credentials exchange and mints the mapped agent 2LO token without a refresh token.

exact.c5.7.jwt-wrong-key.description: A JWT-SVID carrying the configured kid but signed by a key outside the selected trust bundle is rejected even when attacker-controlled jku and x5u header URLs are present.

exact.c5.7.jwt-audience.description: A validly signed JWT-SVID whose audience is not this authorization server is rejected.

exact.c5.7.jwt-issuer-independent.description: A JWT-SVID with an unrelated issuer still succeeds when its sub-derived trust domain, selected bundle signature, audience, and SPIFFE ID policy are valid, proving iss is not the trust anchor.

exact.c5.7.jwt-trust-domain.description: A JWT-SVID from a sub-derived trust domain without a matching tenant binding is rejected even when its signature is otherwise valid.

exact.c5.7.jwt-pattern-negative.description: A valid SPIFFE trust domain cannot authorize a complete SPIFFE ID outside the configured path pattern.

exact.c5.7.jwt-pattern-deep.description: The configured segment-bounded SPIFFE path prefix accepts an authorized deeper workload path.

exact.c5.7.jwt-token-type.description: A token shaped as this authorization server's at+jwt access token cannot be reused as a JWT-SVID.

exact.c5.7.jwt-expiry.description: An expired JWT-SVID is rejected before workload token issuance.

exact.c5.7.jwt-mixed-jwk.description: A trust-bundle JWK mixing EC and RSA key material is rejected instead of selecting an ambiguous verifier.

exact.c5.7.jwt-nbf.description: A JWT-SVID whose nbf is outside the shared clock-skew allowance is rejected.

exact.c5.7.jwt-max-lifetime.description: A validly signed JWT-SVID whose exp minus iat exceeds the shared one-hour platform assertion limit is rejected without a token.

exact.c5.7.jwt-rs256.description: A valid RS256 JWT-SVID from the configured trust bundle completes the same mapped workload exchange as ES256.

exact.c5.7.x509-success.description: A connection carrying an already verified leaf certificate with one authorized SPIFFE URI SAN mints the mapped agent 2LO token without refresh.

exact.c5.7.x509-no-cert.description: The X.509-SVID path does not activate when the trusted client-certificate request extension is absent.

exact.c5.7.x509-exclusive-identity.description: When a verified client certificate is present, the connection identity is authoritative and a conflicting body assertion cannot replace it.

exact.c5.7.x509-binding-negative.description: X.509-SVID identities from another trust domain or outside the configured complete-ID pattern are rejected.

exact.c5.7.x509-san.description: A leaf certificate with no SPIFFE URI identity or with ambiguous multiple URI SANs is rejected.

exact.c5.7.x509-feature-gate.description: A client certificate cannot activate X.509-SVID authentication when the runtime feature gate is disabled.

exact.c5.7.x509-saas-gate.description: The SelfHosted-only X.509-SVID path fails closed for a SaaS issuer even if internal state is constructed with the feature flag enabled.

exact.c5.7.x509-discovery.description: Discovery advertises spiffe_svid_mtls only at P3 with the runtime feature enabled, and omits it at P2 or whenever the gate is off.

exact.c5.7.lambda-client-cert-source.description: Only the API Gateway v2 mTLS requestContext client certificate becomes the trusted ClientCertPem extension; a forged request header is ignored even when it conflicts with the trusted context.

exact.c5.7.mtls-infra.description: Only a P3, feature-enabled SelfHosted deployment creates the versioned private truststore and direct API Gateway mTLS domain, maps it to the token runtime outside CloudFront, and injects the runtime capability; disabled, below-P3, and SaaS deployments create none.

exact.c5.7.jwt-jose.description: A valid ES256 JWT-SVID with the SPIFFE-permitted JOSE typ completes the mapped workload exchange.

exact.c5.7.jwt-audience-array.description: The SPIFFE claims decision accepts an audience array only when it contains this authorization server.

exact.c5.7.jwt-trust-domain-parser.description: SPIFFE trust-domain extraction accepts the scheme authority and rejects empty, port-bearing, userinfo, query, fragment, and non-SPIFFE identities.

exact.c5.7.jwt-subject-shape.description: A client identifier or an empty-trust-domain URI cannot be accepted as a JWT-SVID subject.

exact.c5.7.jwt-pattern-boundaries.description: SPIFFE ID policy supports exact and segment-bounded deep-prefix matches while rejecting empty, bare-wildcard, sibling, and boundary-confusion candidates.

exact.c5.7.jwt-tenant-isolation.description: A valid SPIFFE identity cannot consume an otherwise matching JWT trust binding owned by another tenant.

exact.c5.7.jwt-token-type-case.description: The reserved at+jwt access-token typ is rejected case-insensitively on the JWT-SVID path.

exact.c5.7.jwt-required-claims.description: The SPIFFE claims decision fails closed when required audience or expiry claims are absent.

exact.c5.7.jwt-missing-iat.description: A validly signed JWT-SVID without iat is rejected because its maximum lifetime cannot be bounded.

exact.c5.7.x509-parser-happy.description: The leaf-certificate parser extracts one SPIFFE URI SAN and its validity interval.

exact.c5.7.x509-parser-dns.description: A DNS SAN may coexist with the single SPIFFE URI without becoming part of identity selection.

exact.c5.7.x509-binding-isolation.description: X.509-SVID binding selection rejects cross-domain, pattern-miss, cross-tenant, malformed-subject, and empty-binding cases.

exact.c5.7.x509-mechanism-isolation.description: JWT-SVID and X.509-SVID trust-binding variants cannot satisfy each other's matcher.

exact.c5.7.x509-no-san.description: A leaf certificate without a Subject Alternative Name extension is rejected.

exact.c5.7.x509-no-uri.description: A SAN extension containing no URI identity is rejected.

exact.c5.7.x509-multi-uri.description: A certificate with multiple URI SANs is rejected even when exactly one uses the SPIFFE scheme.

exact.c5.7.x509-non-spiffe-uri.description: A certificate whose only URI SAN does not use the SPIFFE scheme is rejected.

exact.c5.7.x509-malformed-pem.description: Malformed certificate PEM fails closed before identity extraction.

exact.c5.7.x509-validity.description: The application-level defense-in-depth validity check rejects both expired and not-yet-valid X.509-SVIDs without issuing a token.

exact.c5.7.x509-no-assertion-downgrade.description: A copied X.509-SVID PEM submitted as a bearer client_assertion cannot activate the connection-bound mTLS authentication path.

exact.c5.7.jwt-ambiguity.description: Two tenant-scoped JWT-SVID bindings whose trust domain and complete-ID policies both match are rejected instead of selecting a bundle or client by storage order.

exact.c5.7.x509-ambiguity.description: Two X.509-SVID bindings that both match the verified certificate identity are rejected without issuing a token.

exact.c6.1.bare-id.description: A real existing session queried only by identifier returns the same 404 as an unknown identifier.

exact.c6.1.session-token.description: The session bearer grants access only for the matching session-token hash; a wrong bearer returns 404.

exact.c6.1.confidential-owner.description: The owning confidential client authenticates, discovers its session, and queries it through the real HTTP flow.

exact.c6.1.confidential-non-owner.description: A separately authenticated confidential client cannot query another client's real session identifier.

exact.c6.2.constant-time-session-token.description: A structural guard pins the entire real session bearer branch to one HMAC-plus-ConstantTimeEq matcher, excluding alternate variable-time success paths.

exact.c6.2.unified-not-found-body.description: Unknown IDs, bare existing IDs, wrong bearer credentials, and authenticated non-owners all receive the identical 404 response body.

exact.c6.3.exchange-failure-terminal.description: After successful confidential-client authentication, a redirect binding failure atomically consumes the authorization code, advances the bound session sequence exactly once to exchange_failed with structured last_error, and rejects a later correctly bound retry.

exact.c6.3.exchange-failure-conflict.description: A real token request whose bound session changed before the exchange-failure commit returns temporarily_unavailable, preserves the complete session record byte-for-byte, and leaves the code acquirable for retry.

exact.c6.3.exchange-failure-injected.description: An injected atomic-store failure returns temporarily_unavailable while the real HTTP flow leaves both the code unconsumed and the authorization session unchanged in code_issued_awaiting_exchange.

exact.c6.3.exchange-failure-concurrent.description: Concurrent authenticated semantic failures converge to one consumed code and one exchange_failed session, never a split consumed-code/code-issued-session state.

exact.c6.3.confidential-replay-auth.description: After a confidential code exchange succeeds, replay with an invalid client secret cannot revoke the original access token, while replay with the valid bound client authentication returns invalid_grant and makes UserInfo reject that token.

exact.c6.3.bound-replay-revocation.description: A successful public-client exchange remains active across wrong-client, wrong-redirect, and wrong-PKCE replay attempts; only the fully bound replay returns invalid_grant, revokes the refresh family, and makes all UserInfo transports reject the original access token.

exact.c6.3.replay-finalize-race.description: A deterministic pause after code finalization proves that a concurrent fully bound replay suppresses the first token response and revokes the Grant and refresh family created when the first request resumes.

exact.c6.3.replay-rate-limit.description: A fully authenticated and bound code replay bypasses the ordinary issuance bucket after it is exhausted, returns invalid_grant, and still invalidates the original UserInfo access.

exact.c6.3.introspection-revocation.description: Authenticated RS introspection changes the original access token from active true to active false immediately after a fully bound authorization-code replay.

exact.c6.3.dynamo-cancel-retry.description: The production Dynamo exchange-failure transaction classifies a conditional transaction cancellation as transient, preserving the retryable contract instead of reporting a permanent storage failure.

exact.c6.5.authoritative-session-project.description: Creating and advancing a real authorization session persists the final authoritative state at sequence 1 while emitting exactly the matching created(0) and pending_consent(1) projections.

exact.c6.5.dynamo-authority.description: The production Dynamo AuthzSessionStore strongly consistently reads the authoritative record, increments sequence, and conditionally transitions or binds the tenant-scoped state only while the prior sequence matches and expires_at remains later than the authoritative now value.

exact.c6.5.eventbridge-shape.description: The production EventBridge adapter emits the configured bus, stable source and detail type, and exact session_id/sequence/state projection detail.

exact.c6.5.replay-order.description: A deliberately interleaved projection stream partitions by session, prevents equal sequence numbers from colliding across sessions, and deterministically deduplicates and replays each session in ascending sequence order.

exact.c7.1.parameter-contract.description: The RFC 8693 subject and actor token slots require their own values and supported token types; missing, unsupported, and swapped user/workload credentials fail closed.

exact.c7.1.id-token-subject.description: A verified user ID token in the subject_token slot with the ID-token type follows the supported RFC 8693 subject path.

exact.c7.1.access-as-id-mismatch.description: An ES256 at+jwt access token presented in the subject slot while declaring the ID-token type is rejected, completing the bidirectional subject-token type-confusion boundary.

exact.c7.2.actor-allowlist.description: A second workload actor that passes its own client, trust-binding, and platform-JWT authentication is still rejected by the selected Grant actor_allowlist.

exact.c7.2.depth-boundary.description: A valid signed subject with a real JTI/Grant mapping reaches the delegation gate and is rejected when inbound act depth plus the new hop exceeds max_act_chain.

exact.c7.2.may-act.description: The HTTP token-exchange path accepts only a single may_act object whose string sub exactly matches the authenticated actor; rejects wrong, wildcard, array, missing, non-string, and scalar forms; and proves a matching may_act cannot bypass either the independent Grant actor allowlist or max_act_chain gate.

exact.c7.2.no-may-act-output.description: A successful delegation uses the server-side Grant actor_allowlist without copying that allowlist into a may_act claim.

exact.c7.7.mint-contract.description: The owner mints an ES256 grant-ref+jwt with a distinct token type, issuer, grant and agent bindings, matching response/JWT lifetimes fixed at 300 seconds, and no access-token-shaped subject, audience, client, scope, namespace, or actor claims.

exact.c7.7.mint-allowlist.description: The mint endpoint refuses to create a reference bound to an agent outside the selected Grant actor_allowlist.

exact.c7.7.mint-idor.description: An authenticated user cannot mint a reference for another user's Grant and receives the non-enumerating not-found response.

exact.c7.7.mint-auth.description: The grant-reference mint endpoint rejects an unauthenticated caller.

exact.c7.7.leaked-reference.description: A valid leaked reference is rejected when its bound_agent differs from the independently authenticated workload actor presenting it.

exact.c7.7.expired-reference.description: An expired grant reference is rejected before it can select a Grant.

exact.c7.7.type-isolation.description: The dedicated verifier rejects an at+jwt token presented through the grant_ref parameter.

exact.c7.7.not-bearer.description: A valid grant-ref+jwt cannot pass the token-exchange subject or actor verifiers; even with otherwise access-token-shaped claims, real /userinfo and introspection Bearer consumers reject it solely on the dedicated typ.

exact.c7.7.subject-owner.description: A reference for one user's Grant cannot be stitched to another user's subject token even when the actor binding matches.

exact.c7.8.pairwise-target-sector.description: A pairwise subject token is resolved through its JTI mapping to the internal user and exchanged into the exact independently derived target-resource sector subject, distinct from both the internal user id and source-sector subject.

exact.c7.8.unknown-jti.description: A correctly signed pairwise access token whose subject is a valid derivation for a real user but whose JTI is unmapped is rejected rather than trusting, enumerating, or attempting to reverse the subject claim.

exact.c7.8a.missing-jti.description: The ID-token verifier rejects an otherwise valid RS256 ID token that omits the JTI needed for subject and Grant resolution.

exact.c7.8a.unknown-jti.description: A correctly signed ID token with a JTI absent from the mapping store is rejected at the online mapping gate rather than falling back to its subject claim.

exact.c7.8a.missing-grant-pointer.description: An ID-token JTI mapping without the unique grant_id pointer is rejected even when its legacy refresh family remains valid.

exact.c7.8a.access-missing-grant-pointer.description: An access-token JTI mapping without the unique grant_id pointer is rejected under the same rule as ID tokens even when its legacy refresh family remains valid.

exact.c7.8a.source-grant-pointer.description: An ID token mapped to a second source Grant exchanges only for that Grant's resource and reports that Grant in auth_grant, while the default Grant's resource is rejected.

exact.c7.8a.revoked-grant.description: An unexpired ID token cannot exchange after the Grant selected by its JTI pointer has been revoked.

exact.c7.8a.cross-grant-without-ref.description: The presence of another Grant for the same user does not allow an ID token to exchange for that Grant's resource without an explicit grant reference.

exact.c7.8a.cross-grant-with-ref.description: The same ID-token subject can cross to another active Grant only when a grant-ref bound to the authenticated actor selects it, and the output token names that Grant and resource.

exact.c7.9.same-key-rebind.description: A sender-constrained subject token exchanges only when the actor proves possession of the same key, and the delegated token carries that JKT with token_type DPoP.

exact.c7.9.cross-key-rejected.description: A valid proof from a different key cannot launder a stolen sender-constrained subject token into a new delegated token.

exact.c7.9.missing-proof-rejected.description: A subject token carrying cnf.jkt is rejected when the actor provides no DPoP proof, preventing silent downgrade to bearer.

exact.c7.9.actor-proof-opt-in.description: A bearer subject plus an actor proof explicitly opts the delegated token into sender constraint and binds cnf.jkt to the actor key.

exact.c7.9.bearer-default.description: With neither an inbound sender constraint nor an actor proof, token exchange preserves the explicit bearer default and does not invent cnf.

exact.c7.9.required-proof-missing.description: An actor configured with require_dpop cannot exchange a bearer subject without presenting a proof.

exact.c7.9.required-constrained-proof-mi.description: The require_dpop policy combined with an already sender-constrained subject still rejects a missing actor proof and cannot silently downgrade the delegated token to bearer.

exact.c7.9.required-proof-present.description: An actor configured with require_dpop can exchange after presenting a valid proof, and the delegated token is bound to that actor key.

exact.c7.9.malformed-cnf-rejected.description: An inbound cnf object without a string JKT is rejected rather than treated as bearer or rebound to the actor proof.

exact.c7.9.required-cross-key-rejected.description: The require_dpop actor policy does not weaken holder-of-key continuity: a different actor proof key remains rejected for a sender-constrained subject.

exact.c8.11.roundtrip-isolation.description: Real code-flow access tokens read only the namespace selected by their verified audience, return the token subject and namespace revision, and cannot see another resource namespace.

exact.c8.11.strict-gates.description: The RS attributes endpoint ignores a caller-supplied namespace query and fails closed for a wrong token type, bare or multiple audiences, non-user subject type, wrong issuer, absent or expired JTI mapping, a missing JTI store, a JTI authority read error, missing user, disabled or tombstoned user, and unavailable namespace authority.

exact.c8.11.uri-shape.description: Canonical and audience identifiers must be bounded absolute resource URIs without fragments or patterns, preserve case and trailing-slash distinctions byte-for-byte, and enforce the 32-audience maximum.

exact.c8.11.runtime-resolution.description: Exact active bindings resolve to their canonical namespace, mismatched stored URI material and every managed non-active state fail closed, and only a truly unmanaged audience falls back to its raw value.

exact.c8.11.alias-lifecycle.description: Two exact audiences are blocked during migration, share one canonical namespace only after activation, and keep a removed alias fail-closed without raw-key fallback.

exact.c8.11.federation-invalidation.description: A single live RS token sees a federation-owned value at its current enabled mapping revision; update, disable, and delete immediately hide stale values, and the selector directly verifies no-store responses before and after invalidation.

exact.c8.11.federation-target.description: A federation-owned value remains visible only when its current mapping revision also targets the exact canonical namespace and attribute key; same-revision values under another namespace or key are hidden.

exact.c8.11.userinfo-token-rejected.description: An access token whose audience is the issuer userinfo resource is rejected by the independent RS attributes endpoint.

exact.c8.11.userinfo-boundary.description: An access token for an RS remains rejected by userinfo, proving the attributes endpoint does not weaken the C2.11 userinfo audience boundary.

exact.c8.11.saas-first-404.description: Every RS attribute and administration surface returns 404 in SaaS before authentication, query, or body extraction.

exact.c8.1.resource-bound-prm.description: Authenticated RS owners receive PRM documents whose resource exactly preserves the bound identifier including port, path, and trailing slash; close variants and other resources are rejected, and the default AS issuer origin does not publish a global well-known PRM.

exact.c8.1.byod-resource-origin.description: In SelfHosted form with BYOD publication enabled, a registered resource host serves its bound PRM with the configured authorization-server issuer rather than treating the resource host as an issuer.

exact.c8.1.byod-issuer-origin-absent.description: Even while BYOD publication is enabled and another resource host is registered, the AS issuer origin still returns 404 for the protected-resource well-known path.

exact.c8.1b.forwarded-host-overwrite.description: The exact ForwardHost code overwrites an attacker-supplied X-Forwarded-Host with the actual custom-domain viewer Host, and the synthesized distribution attaches that same function at viewer-request plus managed origin authentication at origin-request on the default API behavior.
