exact.c8.1b.saas-host-tenant-binding.description: Through the authenticated managed-edge request shape, two SaaS tenants register distinct BYOD Hosts and public PRM discovery returns only each Host's stored resource and reconstructed tenant issuer. A sibling tenant cannot replace the first global Host binding, and the original response remains unchanged.

exact.c8.1b.owner-derived-from-host.description: The authenticated SaaS tenant is derived from the request Host, and a mismatched or empty body tenant_id cannot redirect ownership of a domain binding.

exact.c8.1b.cross-tenant-unbind.description: A tenant administrator cannot delete another tenant's global domain binding, the rejected operation leaves public PRM discovery intact, and only the owning tenant can remove it.

exact.c8.1b.control-host-rejected.description: The SaaS control Host cannot create a tenant domain binding because it does not establish an authenticated tenant-owner boundary.

exact.c8.1b.unregistered-host.description: A direct-origin request with a forged forwarded Host and missing or invalid managed-edge credential returns 403; with a valid credential, an unregistered viewer Host returns 404 without any tenant PRM fields.

exact.c8.1b.issuer-origin-registration-g.description: SaaS registration rejects the control Host, zone apex, tenant issuer Hosts, and nested issuer subdomains as BYOD resource Hosts.

exact.c8.1b.resource-owner-binding.description: Through the authenticated SaaS edge, domain registration rejects a resource identifier that is not in the tenant owner's registered client resource set.

exact.c8.1b.client-delete-cascade.description: Through the authenticated SaaS edge, deleting the owning client authoritatively removes its global domain binding so subsequent public PRM discovery returns 404 and the tenant can register the Host again.

exact.c7.3.scope-boundary.description: A token-exchange request for a scope outside the selected Grant resource entry is rejected with invalid_scope.

exact.c7.3.resource-boundary.description: A token-exchange request for a resource absent from the selected Grant is rejected with invalid_target.

exact.c7.3.per-resource-scope-boundary.description: A scope granted only for one resource cannot be borrowed for another resource in the same Grant, and the rejected request does not mutate the Grant.

exact.c7.3.selected-grant-scope-boundary.description: A grant_ref exchange rejects a scope outside the Grant selected by the reference instead of authorizing against the source family.

exact.c7.3.selected-grant-resource-bound.description: A grant_ref exchange rejects a resource outside the Grant selected by the reference even when the source family authorizes it.

exact.c7.4.delegated-token.description: A token exchange outside the selected Grant's resource fails without advancing the actor client's activity; the successful exchange advances that actor's last_used_day and returns a delegated token bound to the selected Grant with only its authorized resource and scope. With authz enabled, policy v1 active, the selected Grant stamped at v1, and a policy-artifact read failure armed, the real successful /token exchange performs no artifact read and leaves the failure pending for an explicit cold read.

exact.c7.4.rar.description: The delegated token and its introspection response preserve the selected Grant resource's complete ordered authorization_details constraints instead of truncating or silently widening authority.

exact.c7.4.selected-grant-token.description: A cross-Grant exchange issues a token whose audience, scope, and auth_grant are bounded by the Grant selected through grant_ref.

exact.c7.5.client-policy.description: A client-credentials token receives exactly the resource and default scope registered in the workload client's allowed_resources and allowed_scopes policy.

exact.c7.5.resource-boundary.description: A client-credentials request outside the workload client's allowed_resources policy is rejected with invalid_target.

exact.c7.5.scope-boundary.description: A client-credentials request outside the workload client's allowed_scopes policy is rejected with invalid_scope.

exact.c7.6a.online-offline-boundary.description: After public POST /revoke, refresh is rejected and authenticated introspection becomes inactive immediately, while the same already-issued access token remains valid to the published-JWKS offline verifier through signed exp plus configured clock skew and is rejected at that deterministic boundary.

exact.c7.6a.requires-auth.description: An anonymous revocation request is rejected and leaves the presented refresh family usable.

exact.c7.6a.wrong-secret.description: A confidential client presenting the wrong secret is rejected at the revocation endpoint.

exact.c7.6a.owner-isolation.description: A client attempting to revoke another client's refresh token receives the non-enumerating success response while the owner's family remains usable.

exact.c7.6a.idempotent-no-leak.description: Malformed, unknown, access-token, and repeated revocation inputs all return the same idempotent success response without exposing token existence.

exact.c7.6a.required-token.description: The form-encoded revocation endpoint rejects a request that omits the required token field.

exact.c7.6a.hint-nonsemantic.description: A mismatched but recognized token_type_hint does not change processing: the presented refresh family is still revoked.

exact.c7.6b.grant-cascade.description: The authenticated owner revokes a Grant through the public DELETE endpoint; the authority record becomes revoked, its same-id refresh family is revoked, every cached grace response is removed, and both old and rotated refresh tokens are rejected.

exact.c7.6b.cleanup-retry.description: Injected refresh-family and grace-cache cleanup failures are both attempted and return a retriable error instead of a false success; an idempotent DELETE retry completes both cleanup operations after the Grant is already revoked.

exact.c7.6b.introspection-grant.description: Authenticated introspection changes an otherwise valid access token from active to inactive immediately when its authoritative Grant becomes revoked and exposes no residual token claims.

exact.c7.6b.introspection-family.description: Authenticated introspection also returns inactive when only the associated refresh family is revoked while the Grant remains active, pinning the required two-authority fail-closed decision.

exact.c9.1.per-email-cooldown.description: The public magic-link endpoint sends one message and establishes one per-email cooldown timestamp, then rejects a second request inside the window without advancing the timestamp or enqueueing another message.

exact.c9.1.global-email-quota.description: After the production shared email quota bucket is exhausted, the public endpoint rejects requests for two distinct eligible email addresses without writing either per-email cooldown state or any outbox message.

exact.c9.5.prompt-none-login-required.description: A public authorization request with prompt=none and no login session redirects to the registered client with login_required and never displays the login UI.

exact.c9.5.prompt-none-consent-required.description: An active login session without prior consent receives consent_required under prompt=none and never displays the consent UI.

exact.c9.5.prompt-none-silent-code.description: An active login session with matching prior consent completes prompt=none by redirecting directly to the registered client with a new authorization code.

exact.c9.5.prompt-none-resource-consent.description: Consent granted for an explicit resource cannot be silently reused for a later implicit target: prompt=none returns consent_required and no authorization code.

exact.c9.5.prompt-login-reauth.description: prompt=login ignores an otherwise active session and routes the browser to a fresh login ceremony rather than directly to consent.

exact.c9.5.prompt-none-combination.description: Combining prompt=none with another prompt value is rejected through the registered redirect as invalid_request.

exact.c9.5.max-age-zero.description: max_age=0 rejects reuse of an active session and starts a fresh login ceremony.

exact.c9.5.max-age-authorization-time.description: A session that satisfies max_age when authorization begins can complete consent after that duration elapses, proving freshness is evaluated at the authorization boundary rather than reinterpreted later.

exact.c9.5.max-age-reauthentication.description: A stale session is redirected to login under max_age, and a newly authenticated session resumes the original authorization and produces a code after consent.

exact.c9.5.federation-max-age-forwarding.description: A federated max_age=0 request forwards max_age=0 and prompt=login to the configured upstream IdP while removing the value from the callback continuation so reauthentication does not loop.

exact.c9.5.federation-acr-amr.description: A signed upstream assertion with an explicitly trusted ACR completes the public federation, consent, and token chain; the downstream AS-issued ID token contains the canonical strong ACR and preserves upstream AMR evidence while the access token carries the canonical class.

exact.c9.5.federation-unmapped-acr.description: A strong request forwards the configured upstream ACR, freshness, and reauthentication requirements, then rejects an otherwise signed assertion whose unknown ACR and MFA-shaped AMR are not allowlisted, without creating a session.

exact.c9.5.federation-auth-time.description: A signed assertion with an allowlisted strong ACR but no upstream auth_time cannot satisfy the federated freshness requirement and creates no login session.

exact.c12.1.verifier-storage.description: Newly issued client, registration, and initial-access credential records contain an HMAC-SHA256 verifier rather than plaintext; the verifier is domain-separated by credential kind, tenant, and owner while the record preserves owner, creation, expiry, and active status metadata.

exact.c12.1.auth-method-versioning.description: Disabling and re-enabling client-secret authentication advances the credential version monotonically, rejects a stale stored snapshot, invalidates the old secret, and activates only the newly issued secret.

exact.c12.1.client-secret-rotation.description: Client-secret current and next values overlap, rotation retry never re-discloses plaintext, concurrent cutover has one effective winner, the previous value retires, explicit revoke disables the new value, and audit output contains neither secret nor verifier.

exact.c12.1.client-secret-auto-cutover.description: An elapsed overlap automatically promotes the next client secret, reports its expiry, rejects stale credential snapshots, and never restores the prior secret after revoke or replacement.

exact.c12.1.client-secret-rollback.description: Revoking the staged next client secret during the overlap removes the replacement and its deadline, keeps current usable, records the revoked rotation request for idempotent retry, and advances the credential version.

exact.c12.1.registration-token-rotation.description: Registration access tokens support current and next overlap, cutover, and explicit revoke; both the retired old token and revoked current token are rejected, while Admin responses and credential audit records expose neither token values nor verifiers.

exact.c12.1.registration-token-migration.description: A legacy registration-token hash is lazily replaced by a structured credential record with an explicit verifier version and future expiry, while the plaintext remains absent from the stored record's debug surface.

exact.c12.1.expiry.description: Expired client secrets and expired registration access tokens are rejected by their public authentication boundaries even when the backing records remain present.

exact.c12.1.client-secret-auth-migration.description: Authenticating with a legacy plaintext client secret atomically replaces it with the verifier-backed credential set, preserves the original creation time, assigns an expiry, and removes plaintext from persistent and debug views.

exact.c12.1.client-secret-update-migrati.description: Updating unrelated client metadata also migrates a legacy plaintext secret into versioned verifier storage without returning the secret, rewriting its original creation time, or breaking authentication.

exact.c12.1.storage-migration.description: The production Dynamo adapter transforms a legacy plaintext client secret into an owner-bound HMAC verifier, preserves the legacy registration verifier with its explicit version, writes the versioned credential set, and atomically removes client_secret or reg_token_hash from the same item.

exact.c12.1.iat-lifecycle.description: Initial access tokens persist an audited owner, creation time, fixed expiry, and HMAC verifier; they enforce scope, rate, one-time use, versioned idempotent revoke, rollback by revoking a replacement while the old ticket remains valid, and cutover by revoking the old ticket while the replacement remains valid. Admin list and audit output reveal neither token material nor verifiers.

exact.c12.1.admin-overlap.description: An owner-bound Admin credential set accepts current and next values only during the configured overlap and rejects current at the exact retirement boundary while next remains active.

exact.c12.1.admin-expiry.description: An Admin credential owner with only a not-yet-valid or expired value invalidates the registry and fails authentication closed instead of extending the credential lifetime.

exact.c12.1.admin-owner-isolation.description: Duplicate Admin secret values across owners and a tenant Secret document naming another tenant both invalidate the registry, preventing platform or tenant credentials from crossing ownership boundaries.

exact.c12.1.admin-host-isolation.description: Public Admin routes accept each tenant credential only on its own Host, reject both tenant credentials on the other tenant Host, and reject the platform credential on every tenant Host.

exact.c12.1.admin-revision-regression.description: A warm Admin credential resolver observes a higher revision and immediately accepts only its replacement value, then fails closed if the backing Secret regresses to an older revision.

exact.c12.1.admin-time-immutability.description: A higher Admin credential revision cannot extend an active record's creation or expiry times, move current into next, or extend the retirement boundary of an in-flight rotation.

exact.c12.1.admin-rollback.description: Before retirement, a higher validated revision can roll back an Admin rotation to the prior current value, retires the replacement, and remains stable after the original retirement boundary.

exact.c12.1.admin-rollback-validation.description: A precreated Admin rollback document that was not promoted to the validated stage before retirement is rejected on cold start, so rollback authority cannot be manufactured after the safety window.

exact.c12.1.admin-retired-resurrection.description: A retired Admin credential value cannot be restored as current even by a syntactically higher revision that carries the retired ledger forward.

exact.c12.1.admin-retired-owner-isolatio.description: An Admin credential retired by the platform owner cannot reappear as an active tenant credential, so the append-only retirement boundary is global across configured owners.

exact.c12.1.admin-legacy-lifetime.description: Migrating a legacy Admin bearer starts a bounded lifetime at migration time and serializes a relative TTL so deployment delay cannot silently rewrite its effective creation boundary.

exact.c12.1.admin-copy-migration.description: Admin credential migration copies an unchanged legacy bearer into the owner-bound target document, never mutates the source, and produces the same serialized target across concurrent and interrupted retries before validation.

exact.c12.1.admin-raw-reset.description: Once an Admin target Secret contains a structured owner-bound credential set, replacing it with a raw bearer is rejected rather than downgrading the lifecycle metadata.

exact.c12.1.admin-validated-stage.description: Cold start rejects an Admin Secret with no AGENTAUTH_VALIDATED stage even at revision one, preventing an unvalidated current value from becoming the credential authority.

exact.c12.1.admin-break-glass.description: Public platform, t1, and t2 Admin routes accept their current and next credentials across bounded overlap and reject retired values; every successful use emits exactly one tenant-scoped ADMIN_BREAK_GLASS_USE priority=high event with the used credential_id, and no event logs any bearer value.

exact.c12.1.admin-owner-bound-infra.description: SaaS infrastructure creates distinct platform and tenant Admin target Secrets, publishes only those Admin target references to every runtime, and grants the migration function write and stage-update permissions only on owner-bound targets rather than legacy sources.

exact.c12.1.irreversible-migration-infra.description: The serving stack excludes credential-verifier-v1, while the separate post-deploy stack contains exactly one custom resource with that migration version; the serving stack remains limited to rollback-safe Admin and SCIM Secret copying.

exact.c12.3.group-domain-separation.description: The public SCIM Groups surface rejects directory-supplied role fields, keeps exact CRUD retries idempotent, leaves an unmapped member without a tenant role even when an RS namespace says role=owner, accepts only the four fixed role values through the separate Admin mapping surface, and removes privilege when the mapping or Group is deleted.

exact.c12.3.group-tenant-isolation.description: Two SaaS tenants may reuse directory identifiers while credentials, Group ids, members, mappings, and effective roles remain tenant-local; crossed credentials and member references are rejected without exposing the other tenant.

exact.c12.3.group-stable-generation.description: Effective-role admission accepts only an Active SCIM user whose credential generation is unchanged and has no revocation pending; disabled, pending, or changed-generation observations fail closed.

exact.c12.3.group-idempotence.description: The reference Groups adapter preserves the canonical Group across create retries, grants no role before an explicit mapping, applies fixed-role priority, and removes mapping contributions idempotently.

exact.c12.3.oidc-browser-pkce-binding.description: Admin SSO start preserves an existing authorization-endpoint query, emits every OIDC parameter exactly once, uses a host-only Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax ten-minute flow cookie, stores only the HMAC binding, sends the verifier matching the S256 challenge to token exchange, rejects a copied browser binding, and prevents callback replay from reaching exchange twice.

exact.c12.3.oidc-callback-security.description: The callback atomically consumes flows and creates no session for upstream rejection, missing or invalid keys/signatures, nonce, issuer, audience or time failures, unverified or unknown identity, disabled or pending users, an unmapped Group, or a changed OIDC binding; denial events omit authorization codes, ID/access tokens, secret material, and PKCE verifiers.

exact.c12.3.saas-tenant-oidc.description: Real t1 and t2 SaaS routes use distinct client, redirect, secret-reference, SCIM identity, Group mapping, and session bindings through complete start/callback/session flows; the control host, copied cross-host state, and cross-host session use fail closed.

exact.c12.3.auditor-read-only.description: An attributable auditor OIDC session may read tenant overview and OIDC configuration but cannot reset a password, modify a client, or rotate its credential; all three writes leave authority state unchanged and each records the exact tenant, actor, role, action, and denied result.

exact.c12.3.role-action-matrix.description: Representative real routes fix the complete member, auditor, admin, and owner matrix for session status, tenant read, successful or denied tenant write, and access management, including no-side-effect denials and exact authorization audit results.

exact.c12.3.session-authority-revalidati.description: Fresh control sessions independently fail on OIDC config rebinding or deletion, user disable, completed credential-epoch advance, revocation pending, membership removal, mapping removal, and mapped-role change; clearing only the pending fence restores the matching-generation control session.

exact.c12.3.session-expiry-isolation.description: With valid SaaS config, Active SCIM user, and mapped role controls, a session is accepted before expiry, rejected at the exact expiry boundary, rejected and audited on another tenant host, and deletable only from its owning tenant.

exact.c12.3.logout-persistence.description: An injected persistent session-delete failure returns 503, sends no clearing cookie, and leaves the session usable; a successful retry deletes the record before emitting Max-Age=0 and the old cookie is then rejected.

exact.c12.3.admin-auth-dynamo-routing.description: The production Dynamo adapter routes OIDC configuration through the durable table classification while one-time flows and short-lived sessions route through the Region-local runtime table classification.

exact.c12.3.web-enterprise-sso.description: The SPA exposes the enterprise SSO navigation, follows the mocked browser redirect and callback chain, then enters the Admin workspace without retaining the break-glass token input.

exact.c12.3.web-session-precedence.description: When an OIDC session is active, the SPA removes a stale sessionStorage break-glass token and sends neither the session probe nor subsequent Admin request with an Authorization header.

exact.c12.3.web-auditor-denial.description: The SPA keeps an auditor-visible client after a denied delete and surfaces the authorization failure instead of presenting a successful mutation.

exact.c12.3.scim-groups-infra.description: CDK creates the encrypted PITR SCIM Groups table without TTL, with the tenant-kind index, injects it into exactly the non-token, token, and governance Rust consumers, and grants no non-consumer IAM role table access.

exact.c12.3.admin-sso-infra.description: CDK creates distinct encrypted PITR Admin config and runtime tables, wires both only to the three Rust consumers with matching IAM ownership, publishes their outputs, and retains the dedicated Admin OIDC secret prefix for callback resolution.

exact.c12.4.local-class-mapping.description: The stable canonical baseline and strong ACR values determine local session assurance; passkey-shaped AMR evidence cannot elevate a baseline or missing ACR.

exact.c12.4.policy-actions.description: The default assurance policy requires strong authentication for the literal transfer RAR action and access.manage Admin action while leaving ordinary read actions at baseline.

exact.c12.4.acr-values-step-up.description: A public authorization request for the canonical strong ACR redirects a baseline session to login without a code, preserves acr_values through the continuation, and lets a canonical strong session proceed to consent.

exact.c12.4.amr-no-elevation.description: The public authorization boundary refuses to treat passkey-shaped AMR values as strong when the authoritative session ACR is baseline and issues no authorization code.

exact.c12.4.unknown-acr.description: An authorization request containing only an unknown ACR fails through the registered redirect with unmet_authentication_requirements, preserves state, and issues no code.

exact.c12.4.rar-authorize.description: The public authorization endpoint rejects a browser-controlled login placeholder for a transfer RAR action with unmet_authentication_requirements and no authorization code.

exact.c12.4.rar-consent.description: The transfer RAR strong-assurance requirement is re-evaluated at consent: a baseline session cannot approve a browser-supplied continuation, receives no code, and leaves the authorization session pending authentication.

exact.c12.4.rar-success.description: A baseline session requesting the transfer RAR receives a strong step-up redirect with no code and no Grant. Resuming the same authorization session with canonical strong assurance reaches consent, issues a code and token, and persists the transfer authorization details in both the access token and authoritative Grant.

exact.c12.4.admin-step-up.description: An owner session with unknown ACR and MFA-shaped AMR receives an RFC 9470 insufficient_user_authentication challenge for access.manage and cannot mutate configuration; an unmapped upstream step-up creates no session, while an allowlisted strong step-up succeeds before the mutation.

exact.c12.5.login-session-management.description: The account surface lists only the current user's tenant-scoped login sessions, excludes an OAuth AuthzSession, exposes opaque non-cookie handles, makes crossed and repeated single revocation indistinguishable, retains the current session during bulk revocation, and audits without cookie credentials.

exact.c12.5.current-session-revocation.description: Revoking the opaque handle for the current login session deletes its authority, emits a Max-Age=0 cookie, and rejects the old cookie on the next account request.

exact.c12.5.credential-summary.description: The account summary exposes passkey names, password state, and reauthentication freshness through owner-bound management handles while excluding WebAuthn credential ids, public keys, and counters; a stale session cannot use the handle to rename the passkey.

exact.c12.5.reauthentication-gate.description: At 301 seconds since authentication, passkey rename, passkey deletion, password enrollment, and recovery-material rotation all return the same 300-second reauthentication contract without changing passkey, password, recovery, or login-session authority.

exact.c12.5.password-lifecycle.description: A local user can enroll the first active password and rotate it, each change revokes the acting login session, versions advance monotonically, the old secret stops verifying, and concurrent retry has exactly one committing winner without logging secrets.

exact.c12.5.passkey-management.description: Passkey management handles are owner-scoped, permit naming, reject deletion of the last current-RP factor, ignore a passkey for an obsolete RP, allow deletion only after recovery material exists, revoke the acting session, and keep raw credential ids out of audit.

exact.c12.5.factor-race.description: Concurrent consumption of the last recovery code and deletion of the last passkey linearize so that a passkey, an unused code, or an authoritative recovered session always remains.

exact.c12.5.passkey-registration-reauth.description: Both passkey-registration begin and finish reject a 301-second-old login; rejected finish creates no credential and does not consume the challenge, which the recently authenticated session can still complete.

exact.c12.5.credential-owner-fence.description: The reference authority model refuses password, recovery, and passkey commits unless both the credential epoch and operation id match the active mutation owner, leaving every credential unchanged on mismatch.

exact.c12.5.credential-tombstone-fence.description: Password and recovery commits cannot cross a user tombstone; passkey deletion and credential-fence completion commit together for an active user and both fail without deletion after the user becomes tombstoned.

exact.c12.5.session-dynamo-idempotency.description: The production Dynamo credential-mutation session transaction reuses one idempotency token after a lost committed response and accepts success only when a strong read finds the exact next generation and matching fence id.

exact.c12.5.web-session-management.description: The account UI distinguishes the current login, revokes one other session, signs out all remaining sessions except the current one, and disables the bulk action once no other login remains.

exact.c12.5.web-current-session.description: The account UI confirms current-session revocation, sends the exact handle request, and returns to the login gate after the server removes that login.

exact.c12.5.web-credential-lifecycle.description: The responsive account UI renames an owned passkey, submits a matching first-password enrollment payload, and presents the login gate after the credential change revokes the session.

exact.c12.5.web-password-rotation.description: For an active password, the account UI submits the rotation payload through the change-password control and presents the login gate after session revocation.

exact.c12.5.web-last-factor.description: When the sole passkey has no active password or recovery backup, the UI disables removal and directs the user to add a replacement factor.

exact.c12.5.web-reauthentication.description: A credential mutation denied with reauthentication_required presents the identity-confirmation alert and an exact /login?next=%2Faccount route instead of reporting success.

exact.c12.5.web-recovery-lockout.description: A last_viable_factor recovery-rotation denial keeps the account session active, shows no replacement codes, and explains that an active password or current-site passkey must be added first.

exact.c12.6.event-envelope.description: The canonical event envelope fixes schema 1.0, normalizes the default tenant, preserves typed actor, subject, category, outcome, and correlation fields, and excludes password, recovery-code, client-secret, access-token, and refresh-token fields.

exact.c12.6.key-secret-events.description: Owner-only Admin OIDC configuration and deletion emit successful tenant-scoped KeySecret events without the secret reference, exact-revision deletion invalidates the existing Admin session, and a stale repeated deletion is rejected.

exact.c12.6.event-dedup-export.description: The reference ledger accepts one immutable event id, rejects its exact duplicate, isolates tenant export, orders newest first, applies the requested limit, and binds an opaque continuation cursor to the tenant and time window.

exact.c12.6.delivery-history.description: A typed ingress that failed before reaching the ledger retains its pending, failed, and retrying delivery transitions when the immutable event is finally persisted.

exact.c12.6.admin-export.description: The Admin export rejects an unauthenticated caller and returns only the authenticated tenant's versioned hot-ledger view, retention declaration, delivery history, user-lifecycle event, Admin break-glass event, and denied Admin authentication event.

exact.c12.6.dynamo-ledger.description: The production Dynamo adapter conditionally creates the immutable event and delivery row with the 400-day hot TTL, then queries the tenant/time index consistently without crossing tenant or envelope boundaries.

exact.c12.6.dynamo-reconcile.description: A duplicate immutable event may extend a proven delivery-history prefix through a conditioned update, but an equal-length divergent history is rejected permanently instead of overwriting evidence.

exact.c12.6.ingress-batch.description: SQS batch delivery preserves per-event success, transient failure, and permanent sender-fault classification so one rejected entry cannot suppress successful neighbors or retries for retryable entries.

exact.c12.6.archive-retry.description: An archive write failure records retry history and retries the same immutable event id and deterministic tenant-partitioned object key instead of creating another logical event.

exact.c12.6.archive-terminal.description: When hot-ledger ingress is exhausted, the archive worker preserves the complete typed event and accumulated delivery history in the terminal queue rather than reducing the incident record to an id.

exact.c12.6.event-hot-infra.description: The synthesized stack gives every event-producing runtime the retained PITR-enabled hot ledger, tenant/time and delivery indexes, 400-day TTL, durable SQS fallback, and only the Dynamo and queue permissions needed for idempotent writes and export.

exact.c12.6.event-archive-infra.description: The archive Lambda consumes stream and ingress sources with bounded retry and failure destinations, writes the seven-year tenant archive, uses the terminal FIFO incident queue and scheduled recovery, and has the required table, S3, SQS, and Glue permissions.

exact.c12.6.event-alarm-infra.description: The synthesized deployment retains all event-producing logs for seven years and includes the five security-event alarms, their metric filters and runtime error sources, scoped archive IAM, and operational outputs.

exact.c12.6.ssf-account-projection.description: A successful canonical user.disable event projects to the final RISC account-disabled URI with an exact tenant issuer plus canonical user iss_sub and the immutable event timestamp.

exact.c12.6.ssf-allowlist.description: Projection rejects failed account actions, non-allowlisted user actions, and machine-credential changes, preventing prefix or category-only matching from leaking internal events externally.

exact.c12.6.ssf-session-projection.description: Only an effective single-session revocation projects to the CAEP session-revoked event with a stable opaque session subject; a no-op and revoke-others operation produce no external SET.

exact.c12.6.ssf-credential-projection.description: Passkey create/delete, password set/reset, and recovery rotation project to the CAEP credential-change URI with the exact credential_type, change_type, and immutable event timestamp.

exact.c12.6.ssf-stream-lifecycle.description: A stream is tenant-scoped, publishes only supported delivered events, requires exact revision CAS for replace, pause, resume, and revoke, advances activation on new delivery epochs, and keeps revoked ids as permanent tombstones.

exact.c12.6.ssf-delivery-selection.description: An eligible canonical event creates exactly one tenant-local outbox row only for a current enabled stream after its activation watermark; duplicates, old events, paused streams, other event types, and other tenants create no row.

exact.c12.6.ssf-set-contract.description: The compact SET fixes ES256 and secevent+jwt, issuer, audience, iat, stable jti, txn, RFC 9493 subject, and one event payload, omits forbidden sub and exp, changes identity across stream revisions, and independently verifies against the published JWK selected by kid.

exact.c12.6.ssf-worker-retry.description: A receiver timeout records a retry and the next attempt sends the byte-identical application/secevent+jwt body to the same endpoint until HTTP 202 marks the durable delivery accepted.

exact.c12.6.ssf-retry-exhaustion.description: Repeated receiver 503 responses use one immutable SET across the bounded attempt cycle, record every attempt once, enter dead-letter state exactly at exhaustion, and leave no automatically acquirable due row.

exact.c12.6.ssf-revoke-fence.description: A stream revocation committed after lease acquisition fences subsequent SET persistence, suppresses the outbox row without compact SET material, and prevents any later lease or network delivery.

exact.c12.6.ssf-tenant-keys.description: The SaaS worker signs simultaneous t1 and t2 deliveries with distinct ready tenant key records and each receiver observes only the kid belonging to its delivery tenant.

exact.c12.6.ssf-admin-lifecycle.description: Public tenant Admin routes require access.manage for stream writes, preserve tenant.read for reads, enforce expected revision across create, replace, pause, resume, and revoke, and emit credential-free lifecycle audit events.

exact.c12.6.ssf-admin-key-rotation.description: The Admin stream view exposes only the canonical signing kid, observes a tenant-key rotation through the published key identity, rejects attempts to configure key ARNs, and audits rotation without key material.

exact.c12.6.ssf-admin-outbox.description: Admin verification and terminal redrive use the same tenant-scoped durable outbox, expected stream revision, attempt history, immutable compact SET, 24-hour redrive boundary, and canonical security-event audit path.

exact.c12.6.ssf-saas-scope.description: SaaS t1 and t2 Admin credentials can create and list streams only on their owning tenant Host, while platform, cross-tenant, and control-plane credentials cannot select or observe another tenant's stream records.

exact.c12.6.ssf-metadata-scope.description: Each tenant metadata document publishes spec 1_0, its exact tenant issuer and tenant JWKS origin, push delivery support, and default subjects, while the control Host is rejected as a transmitter issuer.

exact.c12.6.ssf-table-infra.description: The synthesized SSF outbox is tenant-partitioned, retained, PITR-enabled, TTL-governed, and indexed both for active due delivery and immutable stream-revision history, and the Auth runtime receives that exact table.

exact.c12.6.ssf-worker-infra.description: The synthesized SSF worker consumes only new security events, retries due rows every minute, replays retained stream failures through a bounded queue and DLQ, signs with scoped KMS permission, has no destructive table access, and alarms on failure and backlog.

exact.c12.7.user-export.description: The user export requires explicit privacy confirmation, returns the selected tenant's identity and safe metadata, hides active session, passkey, and credential material, and makes a cross-tenant user indistinguishable from a missing user.

exact.c12.7.governance-rbac.description: Governance export actions reject an auditor and a stale Admin session, allow a recently strongly authenticated Admin to export one user, and reserve tenant-wide export for a strongly authenticated owner.

exact.c12.7.tenant-export-redaction.description: Tenant configuration, secret metadata, and signing-key export sections carry residency and revision context while excluding secret references, fingerprints, key ARNs, and public key material.

exact.c12.7.legal-hold-resume.description: A revisioned legal hold blocks erasure and offboarding, release resumes the same durable jobs without duplicate work, and the offboarding lifecycle fence rejects later ordinary and background-authority mutations while preserving discovery.

exact.c12.7.post-primary-hold.description: A hold introduced after primary user cleanup stops replica verification, release resumes the same suppression-bound job, retention remains explicit, and terminal retries do not enqueue another destructive operation.

exact.c12.7.continuation.description: The platform continuation path remains usable after tenant Admin authority is removed, binds one signed token to tenant, job, action, and expiry, rejects replay, and retrieves only the matching job evidence.

exact.c12.7.user-erasure.description: User erasure advances through every durable phase, removes canonical identity, aliases, sessions, credentials, Grants, protocol artifacts, and Group membership, prevents suppressed recreation, waits for retention, and publishes redacted completion evidence.

exact.c12.7.offboarding-legacy-tombstone.description: Tenant offboarding safely adopts a legacy zero-epoch tombstoned identity into a fenced child erasure instead of skipping it or treating its old epoch as current authority.

exact.c12.7.offboarding-resume.description: Tenant offboarding persists immutable pagination and child-job state across restarts, removes tenant users and dependent authority without skipping the first page, and settles external resources with explicit verified outcomes.

exact.c12.7.stale-worker-hold.description: A legal-hold policy revision committed after job creation fences the stale erasure worker before its first mutation, preserves the user, and requires an explicit release before the same job can continue.

exact.c12.7.secondary-region.description: A configured secondary residency Region may serve tenant export and policy reads with explicit active-writer and governance Region context, but rejects destructive governance work outside the designated governance Region.

exact.c12.7.residency-config.description: The runtime residency parser requires an exact tenant set, non-empty unique allowed Regions, and a governance Region that belongs to the tenant's allowed set.

exact.c12.7.suppression-domain.description: Governance suppression digests are domain-separated by tenant and alias kind so the same plaintext cannot correlate across tenants or alias namespaces.

exact.c12.7.retention-deadline.description: The governance worker derives a conservative retention deadline that covers the security-event archive, hot ledger, shared backup window, and incident queues instead of reporting physical deletion early.

exact.c12.7.retention-region.description: Multi-Region retention completion runs only in the active governance Region and binds evidence to the configured replicas, active writer revision, and declared AWS Backup policy window.

exact.c12.7.retention-atomic.description: A storage failure during final retention completion exposes neither a completed job nor partial evidence, preserving the atomic boundary between deletion state and proof.

exact.c12.7.governance-authorities-infra.description: The governance job and suppression authorities are retained, deletion-protected, PITR-enabled for 35 days, replicated, stream-enabled, and the suppression ledger has no TTL.

exact.c12.7.runtime-suppression-access-i.description: The serving runtime receives residency and governance secrets only through versioned bootstrap configuration and has condition-read but no mutation access to the non-rollback suppression authority.

exact.c12.7.governance-worker-infra.description: The durable FIFO governance worker has bounded retries, complete authority and retention inventory, scoped destructive permissions, append-only suppression access, alarms, and an hourly retention schedule.

exact.c12.7.backup-excludes-control-infr.description: Ordinary business-authority backup excludes the current governance and suppression control tables while retaining alarms for their health and replication.

exact.c12.7.background-writers-infra.description: Every background authority writer receives the same governance bootstrap, suppression, queue, deployment, and transaction-fence permissions as interactive writers.

exact.c12.7.residency-deployment-infra.description: CDK synthesis fails when residency does not cover the exact SaaS tenant set or names storage Regions outside the deployed topology.

exact.c12.7.recoverable-authority-infra.description: Production recovery retains and gives 35-day PITR to safe durable authority while transient replay, session, verifier, outbox, and rate-limit tables remain non-restorable; current non-rollback controls are retained separately.

exact.c12.7.daily-backup-infra.description: The production profile creates an encrypted retained vault, daily 05:00 backup with a 35-day lifecycle, selects only safe authority tables, grants a backup-only role, and exports deployment and table identity.

exact.c12.7.backup-deadline-infra.description: The live governance drill accepts only completed recovery points whose configured 35-day lifecycle also has a concrete provider-calculated deletion deadline.

exact.c12.7.export-cursor-infra.description: The live tenant-export verifier follows bounded opaque cursors, rejects cursor loops, URL-encodes continuation values, and proves the expected user appears in the returned records.

exact.c12.7.offboarding-live-counts-infr.description: The live offboarding verifier uses strongly consistent paginated scans and nested-record matching for tenant and user authority instead of treating one page or a GSI count as absence evidence.

exact.c12.7.replica-zero-count-infra.description: Service evidence must enumerate every configured replica, identify provider strong reads, carry verification timestamps, and report zero live counts in each Region before completion.

exact.c12.7.retention-exception-infra.description: The governance drill requires evidence to declare external_operator_managed retention exceptions rather than claiming the product preserved operator-owned legal-hold resources.

exact.c12.7.secret-ownership-infra.description: Secret cleanup evidence binds persisted ownership metadata, distinguishes product-managed pending deletion from verified external retention, and rejects unexpected ownership counts.

exact.c12.7.verifier-control-authority-i.description: The restore verifier keeps current governance and suppression authority, rejects table aliasing, requires cross-Region convergence, and fails when either control authority changes during candidate verification.

exact.c12.7.verifier-strong-read-infra.description: The restore verifier scans candidate and control tables with consistent reads and contains no DynamoDB, KMS, or Secrets Manager destructive command.

exact.c12.7.verifier-business-roles-infr.description: The restore verifier enumerates all twelve recoverable business roles and invokes the pure verifier with the manifest and versioned suppression HMAC key.

exact.c12.7.verifier-evidence-infra.description: Restore evidence is published atomically after temporary data cleanup, excludes HMAC keys, suppression digests, user identifiers, and account ids, and includes only hashed account identity.

exact.c12.7.live-cutover-roles-infra.description: The live cutover gate requires explicit confirmation, restores exactly twelve named roles at one bounded PITR cutoff, and derives that cutoff from current restorable epochs.

exact.c12.7.live-cutover-provenance-infr.description: The live gate requires a clean harness commit, verifies deployment ancestry and byte-identical verifier files, and runs the deployed verifier from a detached worktree.

exact.c12.7.live-cutover-cleanup-infra.description: Live cleanup binds deterministic target names to restore receipts, table identity, source ARN, CloudTrail acceptance, stable absence, and stack-policy receipts before deleting isolated candidates.

exact.c12.7.live-cutover-publication-inf.description: PASS evidence is published only after pure verifier success, deletion of every isolated table, restoration of the deployment freeze, and hashing of all deployment and receipt provenance.

exact.c12.7.live-cutover-resume-infra.description: Restart-safe resume rejects changes to stack identity, deployment commit, current source-table map, source table ids, or creation times.

exact.c12.7.live-cutover-ambiguous-infra.description: Live restore polling distinguishes confirmed absence from ambiguous control-plane errors and fails closed when the ambiguity does not resolve.

exact.c12.7.restore-clean.description: The pure restore verifier accepts a complete clean candidate only when users, passkeys, password credentials, Grants, and Group memberships preserve referential integrity.

exact.c12.7.restore-user-suppression.description: Canonical-id, email, SCIM external-id, and SCIM user-name suppression records each reject a restored erased user.

exact.c12.7.restore-tenant-suppression.description: Either permanent tenant suppression or an offboarding lifecycle rejects any restored live business authority for that tenant.

exact.c12.7.restore-retained-controls.description: The restore verifier distinguishes retained security events and a fully settled offboarded tenant-key control row from live business authority.

exact.c12.7.restore-dangling-reference.description: A restored credential or authorization record that references a missing canonical user fails cutover rather than being accepted as partial authority.

exact.c12.7.restore-key-version.description: A suppression entry whose HMAC key version is unavailable fails closed instead of treating an unverifiable digest as absence.

exact.c12.7.restore-unknown-tenant.description: Restored business authority with a tenant prefix outside the current manifest fails closed.

exact.c12.7.restore-transient-admin.description: Transient Admin flows, sessions, and unknown Admin authority row types in a restored durable table fail cutover.

exact.c12.7.restore-incomplete-scan.description: A candidate scan with an unconsumed LastEvaluatedKey is rejected so one page cannot be mistaken for complete absence.

exact.c12.7.restore-malformed-audit.description: Malformed retained security-event identifiers and tenant fields fail cutover instead of being broadly exempted as audit data.

exact.c12.2.core-flow.description: The public SCIM Users API preserves one canonical identity across create retry, direct GET, filtered lookup, and full PUT replacement while returning the profile schemas and media types required by the supported profile.

exact.c12.2.lifecycle-epoch.description: SCIM disable and re-enable advance the lifecycle epoch, revoke the prior sessions, refresh families, Grants, and credentials, and never make artifacts from an older epoch valid again.

exact.c12.2.tombstone-retry.description: An exact POST retry cannot rebind a tombstoned canonical identity or its externalId and userName aliases.

exact.c12.2.tenant-isolation.description: SCIM credentials, canonical IDs, externalId and userName aliases, filters, and idempotent retries remain isolated between tenants.

exact.c12.2.okta-flow.description: The real-Okta acceptance harness drives assignment, deprovisioning, re-provisioning, identity preservation, final cleanup, private evidence, and checksum production without exposing either provider credential.

exact.c12.2.okta-cleanup-failure.description: A failed Okta fixture cleanup prevents the harness from writing successful acceptance evidence.

exact.c12.2.okta-run-id.description: Unsafe run identifiers are rejected before any Okta or Agent Auth provider call.

exact.c12.2.okta-secret-injection.description: A SCIM credential containing header-control bytes is rejected before any provider request or evidence write.

exact.c12.2.okta-preexisting-user.description: The harness refuses to reuse or delete a pre-existing Okta directory identity.

exact.c12.2.okta-evidence-reservation.description: An existing evidence path is preserved and blocks a new provider run instead of being overwritten.

exact.c12.2.okta-create-collision.description: A provider-side create collision cannot make cleanup delete a directory user whose ownership was never confirmed.

exact.c12.2.okta-interrupt-cleanup.description: An interrupted run deletes only its confirmed disposable Okta user and produces no success evidence.

exact.c12.2.okta-lock-contention.description: Evidence lock contention fails before provider calls and never removes another run's reservation.

exact.c13.8.malformed-form.description: A malformed EMA token request returns OAuth invalid_request with HTTP 400 and Cache-Control no-store.

exact.c13.8.permanent-failure.description: A permanent signer failure after replay consumption returns HTTP 500 server_error with no-store, no Retry-After, no assertion, issuer, subject, or token material, and leaves the assertion consumed.

exact.c12.8.evidence-assembly.description: Release evidence combines the project RFC 9700 regression, official OIDF suite result, exact issuer and deployment commit, start/end deployment preflights, requested profile claim, and exception list into one gate input.

exact.c12.8.oidf-export.description: The official Basic OP plan converter requires the complete discovery plus dynamic-client module set, records runner status and module count, verifies every exported signature, and preserves the upstream PASSED/WARNING results instead of laundering them.

exact.c12.8.oidf-origin.description: An otherwise complete official-plan export from any origin other than the pinned OIDF conformance server is rejected before it can become release evidence.

exact.c12.8.oidf-signature.description: Tampering with a signed OIDF export member makes conversion fail closed, so unsigned or signature-invalid plan results cannot enter the release gate.

exact.c12.8.gate-pass.description: Passing pinned project and official suites for the preflight-bound issuer and deployment produce a schema-v2 authorization limited to oidc-basic-op-code, valid for the policy evidence window, with FAPI and OpenID Federation explicit non-claims.

exact.c12.8.gate-failure.description: A required RFC 9700 regression failure makes the release gate fail, reports the exact suite/test identifier, and produces no approved profile claims artifact.

exact.c12.8.exception-pass.description: Only an exception bound to the exact failed suite/test with approver, approval time, reason, issue, and unexpired bounded lifetime can waive that result while remaining reported as waived.

exact.c12.8.invalid-evidence.description: The gate rejects missing suites or versions, deployment drift, stale evidence, wrong plan variants or pinned runner commit, false upstream success, cleanup defects, runner failure, duplicate results, and attempts to claim unapproved optional profiles.

exact.c12.8.invalid-exceptions.description: Expired, future-dated, overlong, unowned, untracked, duplicate, unused, or otherwise malformed exception records fail closed and cannot authorize a release claim.

exact.c12.8.workflow-chain.description: The actual release workflow runs deployment preflight, protected OIDF configuration and live probes, the project RFC 9700 regression, the pinned official runner, a post-suite deployment check, and evidence assembly in fail-closed order.

exact.c12.8.workflow-promotion.description: The actual scheduled release workflow is explicitly enabled, invokes promotion validation, tracks non-successful external gates, and removes approved claims when sensitive evidence packaging fails before artifact upload.

exact.c12.8.promotion-pass.description: Promotion accepts an unexpired approved artifact only when its evidence digest, policy digest, issuer, deployment commit, approved profile, and explicit non-claims all match.

exact.c12.8.promotion-reject.description: Promotion rejects expired authorization, issuer or deployment mismatch, evidence or policy digest drift, missing explicit non-claims, and any required profile that the gate did not approve.

exact.c12.8.exception-issue-binding.description: Every release exception is verified against the configured repository, an open issue body binding the exact target and expiry, the approval label, and the matching allowed approver label event.

exact.c12.8.monitor-fresh.description: The continuous watchdog accepts a configured deployment only when the latest scheduled external gate completed its required job successfully and the resulting evidence is still inside the policy age window.

exact.c12.8.monitor-config-skipped-stale.description: A missing deployment commit, a skipped required external job, and evidence older than the policy window are independently reported instead of treating a nominally successful workflow shell as current conformance evidence.

exact.c12.8.monitor-runner.description: A scheduled gate that remains queued or active beyond the external job runtime boundary reports the dedicated runner as potentially unavailable and does not refresh stale success evidence.

exact.c12.8.monitor-schedule.description: Absence of any scheduled release-conformance run is reported together with absence of successful scheduled evidence.

exact.c12.8.monitor-issue.description: The watchdog creates one stable tracker issue for active findings and closes that open tracker after recovery without interpolating findings into shell source.

exact.c12.8.monitor-workflow.description: The independent GitHub-hosted watchdog runs every three hours with only Actions read, contents read, and issues write permissions, consumes repository conformance configuration, and never enters the secret-bearing conformance environment.

exact.c12.8.complete-row-gate.description: A checked conformance row cannot lose all exact automated targets and degrade to report-only coverage; evidence-map validation fails before CI can pass.

exact.c9.2.browser-nonce-binding.description: A magic link opened with a different browser nonce is rejected without creating a login session or consuming the link; the initiating browser then redeems the same link and receives a login session.

exact.c9.2.dynamo-bound-consume.description: The production Dynamo adapter reads the tenant-partitioned link strongly, conditionally deletes only for the bound browser nonce, returns the consumed record once, maps conditional conflicts to no result, and fails closed on other errors.

exact.c9.6.get-logout.description: GET /end-session deletes the authoritative session, clears the host-only cookie with matching attributes, and the old session can no longer authorize a request.

exact.c9.6.post-logout.description: POST /end-session provides the form-body alternative and clears the same authoritative session cookie.

exact.c9.6.invalid-hint.description: Malformed, signature-tampered, expired, and explicit-client audience-mismatched ID-token hints are rejected before session deletion, preventing an attacker from forcing another browser to log out.

exact.c9.6.valid-hints.description: Valid default RS256 and configured ES256 ID-token hints establish the registered client, permit its exact post-logout redirect with state, and terminate the authoritative browser session.

exact.c9.6.redirect-exact.description: Post-logout redirects require byte-for-byte registration: foreign, scheme-case, host-case, default-port, trailing-slash, query, fragment, and percent-encoding variants are rejected while local logout still completes; the exact registered URI redirects and echoes state.

exact.c9.6.no-client-local-logout.description: When no client identity can be established, the AS refuses to follow the supplied redirect while deleting the authoritative server session and clearing the browser cookie.

exact.c9.3.generate-auth.description: The public recovery-generation endpoint rejects an unauthenticated caller before issuing recovery material.

exact.c9.3.generate-show-once.description: Authenticated generation returns ten show-once codes, persists only server-secret HMAC values, exposes only configured/remaining status afterward, and regeneration replaces every old code while leaving the new set usable.

exact.c9.3.contact-channel.description: Generation and recovery fail closed for missing, invalid, or unavailable canonical contact-email authority; no code is consumed and an internal canonical user ID is never used as a notification recipient.

exact.c9.3.replay-session.description: A lost-response retry replays only the originally committed recovery session without advancing authority again; deleting that session restores one-time rejection while another unconsumed code remains usable.

exact.c9.3.replay-password-authority.description: A committed recovery result cannot replay after a temporary-password reset makes the recovered session ineligible.

exact.c9.3.replay-user-authority.description: A committed recovery result cannot replay after the canonical user's credential authority epoch changes.

exact.c9.3.pending-fence.description: A pending credential mutation rejects recovery before code consumption, and the same code succeeds after the authoritative fence completes.

exact.c9.3.last-viable.description: A recovery-only session without an active password or current-RP passkey receives last_viable_factor while preserving both its authoritative session and existing recovery material.

exact.c9.3.passkey-backup.description: A current-RP passkey is accepted as the non-recovery backup factor that permits a recovery-only session to rotate its recovery material.

exact.c9.3.operation-id.description: The public recovery endpoint requires an unpadded canonical base64url operation ID decoding to exactly 32 bytes and rejects missing, short, or padded values.

exact.c9.3.lockout.description: Repeated user-scoped wrong recovery-code attempts reach the public lockout response, after which even the correct code receives 429 with no recovery session.

exact.c9.3.lockout-boundary.description: The recovery state machine keeps attempts one through four unlocked, locks exactly on attempt five for 900 seconds, remains locked through the final prior second, and unlocks at the exact boundary.

exact.c9.3.refresh-revocation.description: Recovery-material rotation and successful recovery keep all existing refresh families revoked and remove stale grace responses.

exact.c9.3.session-revocation.description: Recovery-material rotation immediately invalidates prior sessions, and successful recovery also invalidates a session established after rotation.

exact.c9.3.status-auth.description: The recovery-status endpoint rejects unauthenticated callers.

exact.c9.3.status-counts.description: Authenticated recovery status reports unconfigured, ten generated codes, and nine remaining after one successful consumption without returning recovery plaintext.

exact.c9.3.status-isolation.description: Recovery status is derived only from the authenticated user and does not disclose another user's configured state or remaining count.

exact.c9.3.generate-rate.description: Repeated recovery generation exhausts the authenticated user's bucket with 429 while a different user's independent bucket remains available.

exact.c9.3.dynamo-rotation.description: Production Dynamo recovery rotation atomically completes the canonical-user credential fence and writes only hashed recovery entries, replaying an ambiguous transaction byte-for-byte with the same idempotency token.

exact.c9.3.dynamo-notification.description: Production Dynamo notification persistence derives a tenant-scoped recovery message key so replaying the same recovery operation records one notification.

exact.c9.3.dynamo-success.description: Production Dynamo sends one six-item transaction that email- and epoch-fences the canonical user, consumes the verifier, checks password authority, advances session generation, writes the recovery session, and writes a code-bound 60-second result; ambiguous responses reuse the same token and the committed result remains recoverable.

exact.c9.3.expired-result.description: A recovery result at its 60-second expiry boundary cannot replay a session or issue a cookie.

exact.c9.3.web-operation-id.description: The recovery page generates a canonical 32-byte base64url operation ID, reuses it after an ambiguous 503, and replaces it only after a definitive rejection.

exact.c9.3.web-show-once.description: The account UI preserves newly returned show-once recovery codes across session revocation and a dismissed navigation warning, then removes them only after explicit saved-code acknowledgement.

exact.c9.7.no-jit-suppression.description: The public magic-link endpoint gives an unknown email the same status, JSON keys, sent flag, callback path, and complete query-key sequence as an eligible Active user without creating a user or outbox message; the synthetic callback is unredeemable and creates no session. An Admin-provisioned temporary credential receives the generic response but no outbox delivery, and its synthetic callback is likewise unredeemable without a session.

exact.c9.8.infra-store.description: The synthesized deployment creates exactly one encrypted, PITR-enabled password credential table keyed by user_id without DynamoDB TTL, wires only its name to the non-token Auth runtime, grants that runtime the table ARN, and retains memory headroom for the bounded Argon2 workers.

exact.c9.8.password-policy.description: Password policy measures the submitted UTF-8 bytes without trimming and enforces the inclusive reviewed 12-to-128-byte boundary.

exact.c9.8.salted-argon2.description: Two hashes of the same compliant password are distinct because each uses a fresh cryptographic salt; the correct password verifies and an incorrect password does not.

exact.c9.8.phc-profile.description: Verification rejects malformed PHC values and hashes whose Argon2 memory cost differs from the fixed reviewed profile before spending an attacker-selected resource budget.

exact.c9.8.storage-profile.description: The storage boundary accepts only the exact Argon2id v19 profile with m=19456, t=2, p=1, a 32-byte output, and the reviewed minimum salt encoding.

exact.c9.8.dynamo-store.description: The production Dynamo adapter writes only the tenant-prefixed user key, PHC hash, lifecycle flags, operation marker, version, and timestamp; the cleartext never reaches the request, and reads use the exact tenant-prefixed key with ConsistentRead=true.

exact.c9.8.memory-store.description: The in-memory authority model isolates identical users across tenants, permits exactly one version-and-must-change CAS activation, monotonically advances reset versions, rejects conflicting retries, and keeps the other tenant unchanged.

exact.c9.8.scim-version-fence.description: A SCIM-created user with a random canonical identifier is provisioned and reset through its current email alias; the credential remains bound to the canonical user, advances version, invalidates the old authority version, and revokes the existing session.

exact.c9.8.admin-reset.description: Admin reset rejects reuse of the active password, atomically installs a new temporary version, advances credential authority, revokes old sessions and refresh state without revoking the Grant, redacts the secret and PHC hash, and makes exact retry idempotent.

exact.c9.8.code-version-fence.description: After reset and mandatory password change, both a pre-reset authorization code carrying the old password version and a legacy password-capable code lacking the version fail at the public token endpoint with invalid_grant.

exact.c9.8.device-ciba-reset-fence.description: Approved Device and CIBA artifacts snapshot the active password credential version; after Admin reset and mandatory password change, both public token grant paths reject those pre-reset approvals with invalid_grant.

exact.c9.8.legacy-refresh-fence.description: A password-capable user's legacy refresh family without a password credential version is rejected with invalid_grant before its Region-local family version rotates.

exact.c9.8.legacy-device-fence.description: An approved legacy Device grant for a password-capable local user that lacks the password credential version returns invalid_grant and remains unconsumed.

exact.c9.8.legacy-ciba-fence.description: An approved legacy CIBA request for a password-capable local user that lacks the password credential version returns invalid_grant and remains unconsumed.

exact.c9.8.reset-eligibility.description: Admin may pre-provision a Disabled local identity but it cannot log in; missing, Tombstoned, and federated users are rejected without leaving password credentials.

exact.c9.8.partial-write-recovery.description: A fail-closed credential-first partial Admin create cannot authenticate or send magic links, rejects a retry with a different secret, and lets an exact retry finish canonical user creation without rewriting the password version.

exact.c9.8.pending-alias-fence.description: A pending initial password remains fail closed after its SCIM alias moves; login and change cannot use it until an exact Admin retry resolves the new alias to the same canonical user and clears only the owned pending marker.

exact.c9.8.legacy-session-revocation.description: Adding an initial temporary password to an existing local user revokes a legacy passwordless login session before the credential becomes usable.

exact.c9.8.tombstone-cleanup.description: Admin provisioning against a Tombstoned canonical user returns conflict and conditionally removes the stale password credential rather than reviving it.

exact.c9.8.markerless-pending-reset.description: A legacy reset row that is temporary and revocation-pending but lacks its durable operation marker cannot complete a password change or be adopted by a new Admin reset.

exact.c9.8.aws-reset-reconciliation.description: The production Dynamo Admin-reset stage reuses one transaction token after a lost committed response, then performs one strong read of the user and password authority rows and reconciles only the exact operation, hash, and version.

exact.c9.9.authz-session-gate.description: A correct temporary password returns change-required with no login session, unexpired authorization code, or Grant and leaves the authorization session pending user authentication; only a successful password change creates exactly one amr=pwd login session and advances the authorization session to pending consent.

exact.c9.9.concurrent-change.description: Two concurrent first-password changes against the same version and must-change credential produce exactly one successful activation, one conflict, one session cookie, one authoritative amr=pwd login session, and one active version-2 credential. With one account-failure token remaining, neither the successful change nor the CAS loser consumes it: the next invalid credential receives 401 and only the following request receives 429 with Retry-After.

exact.c9.10.dummy-profile.description: The embedded unknown-account dummy hash is accepted only through the reviewed Argon2id PHC profile and performs a real unsuccessful password verification.

exact.c9.10.success-budget.description: Repeated correct temporary-password checks continue returning change-required beyond the account failure capacity, and repeated successful active-password logins continue returning authenticated sessions beyond that capacity, proving both valid outcomes leave the invalid-credential budget untouched.

exact.c9.10.failure-budget.description: Five invalid password attempts consume the account failure budget and the next attempt is rejected with 429 and a positive Retry-After header.

exact.c9.10.trusted-source-ip.description: An exhausted trusted-source-IP bucket rejects a request with 429 and positive Retry-After even when the caller supplies a different X-Forwarded-For value, proving the public endpoint does not key the password limit from the forgeable header.

exact.c9.10.tenant-isolation.description: Exhausting the password-attempt tenant bucket for one SaaS tenant returns 429 with positive Retry-After there while another tenant remains admitted; exhausting one tenant's trusted-source-IP bucket likewise leaves the same trusted IP independently admitted in the other tenant.

exact.c9.10.global-budget.description: Once the deployment-global password bucket is exhausted, requests in two distinct SaaS tenants using unrelated email addresses both receive 429 with positive Retry-After, proving tenant and email rotation cannot evade the shared deployment budget.

exact.c9.10.store-fail-closed.description: With the rate-limit dependency unavailable, a valid provisioned password is rejected with 503 before authentication and no authoritative login session is created.

exact.c9.10.worker-saturation.description: Holding every bounded password-verification worker permit makes unknown, unconfigured, wrong-password, Disabled, and Tombstoned identities all return 503 within a one-second bound without creating canonical or fallback authoritative sessions.

exact.c9.10.spawn-blocking.description: A structural guard requires one bounded worker permit before each single hash or verify call inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, fixes one alias read, one credential read, and one verification before all authentication outcome branches, and uses a Rust AST guard to forbid every macro in the hash, verify, login, and password-change bodies while allowing only the reviewed fallback-id format macro in authenticate.

exact.c9.10.change-shared-gates.description: The public password-change endpoint consumes the same account, trusted-source-IP, tenant, and deployment-global attempt buckets as login; after each final token is consumed, a subsequent request returns 429 with positive Retry-After before a fully occupied Argon2 worker gate and creates no authoritative session.

exact.c9.10.alias-success.description: After a SCIM email alias moves to the same canonical user, the old address performs one fallback credential read and is rejected, while the new address performs one alias read, uses only the canonical credential key before verification and during the later session-authority recheck, authenticates with the existing password, and keeps Admin reset bound to that canonical user.

exact.c9.10.alias-failure-fixed-read.description: An injected alias-store failure makes the public password endpoint return 503 after exactly one alias read and exactly one fallback credential read, without creating canonical or fallback sessions.

exact.c9.10.rate-store-errors.description: Injected rate-limit errors in both the pre-authentication availability check and the invalid-credential account consume path return 503 and create no authoritative session.

exact.c9.10.dynamo-retry-exhaustion.description: The production Dynamo rate-limit adapter performs five strong reads and five conditional writes under repeated CAS conflicts, then returns a transient store error instead of admitting the request.

exact.c9.10.lambda-source-ip.description: The production build_router wiring exposes API Gateway v2 requestContext.http.sourceIp as TrustedSourceIp even beside a conflicting X-Forwarded-For header, causing the real password route to hit the trusted-IP bucket; after the X-Forwarded-For-derived bucket is separately exhausted, an X-Forwarded-For-only request still receives no trusted source IP.

exact.c9.10.account-hmac.description: Account-bucket keys are deterministic for one tenant/email pair, differ across tenants, emails, and configured server secrets, remain tenant scoped, contain no email PII, and a fixed known-answer vector pins the keyed HMAC-SHA-256 domain/NUL/tenant/NUL/email input sequence.

exact.c9.10.parameter-failure-budget.description: With one account-failure token remaining, same-password and weak-new-password rejections after valid current-password authentication create no session and consume no failure budget; the next invalid credential receives 401 and only the following request receives 429 with Retry-After.

exact.c9.10.session-failure-budget.description: With one account-failure token remaining, injected authoritative-session persistence failures after a valid active-password login and after a successful first-password CAS each return 503, create no session, and consume no failure budget; in both flows the next invalid credential receives 401 and only the following request receives 429.

exact.c9.10.secret-wrappers.description: Compile-time negative trait assertions prevent PasswordValue from implementing Debug, Clone, or Serialize and prevent EncodedPasswordHash from implementing Debug or Serialize; a structural guard also requires PasswordValue Drop to zeroize the cleartext buffer exactly once.

exact.c9.10.body-limit.description: Both public password login and password-change routes accept an exact 4096-byte JSON body and reach authentication, reject 4097 bytes with 413, and return Cache-Control: no-store; malformed JSON is likewise a no-store client error.

exact.c9.7.admin-provisioned-login.description: A user created through the authenticated Admin endpoint completes the password activation ceremony and then signs in through the public magic-link flow under the same canonical user id; authenticated Admin detail proves the magic-link session advances last_login_at beyond the password-session baseline.

exact.c9.7.disabled-no-send.description: Disabling a canonical user rejects a previously issued link without a session and preserves the prior last_login_at; a separate user disabled before its first magic-link request receives the same status, content type, JSON keys, sent flag, callback path, and complete query-key sequence as an eligible Active user without an outbox message, and the synthetic callback cannot authenticate.

exact.c9.7.tombstoned-no-revival.description: Tombstoning rejects a previously issued link and prevents Admin create or enable revival; a separate user tombstoned before its first magic-link request receives the same status, content type, JSON keys, sent flag, callback path, and complete query-key sequence as an eligible Active user without an outbox message, and the synthetic callback cannot authenticate.

exact.c9.7.alias-binding.description: A link issued to one canonical user remains bound to that user: after the email alias moves and is assigned to a replacement user, callback redemption is forbidden and no replacement-owner session is created.

exact.c9.7.password-no-jit.description: The public password endpoint gives unknown, unconfigured, wrong-password, Disabled, and Tombstoned identities the same no-store 401 response without canonical or HMAC-fallback sessions, and an unknown email remains absent from the authoritative user store. With one account-failure token remaining, each invalid outcome consumes that final token and the next request returns 429 with positive Retry-After.

exact.c9.7.passkey-no-jit.description: Public passkey authentication for an unknown email exposes no credentials; valid signed assertions from orphaned credentials with both user-prefixed and arbitrary canonical owner ids are rejected because the canonical UserRecord is missing, while an existing Active arbitrary canonical owner at nonzero lifecycle epoch authenticates successfully and anonymous registration remains unauthorized.

exact.c9.7.passkey-postwrite-status.description: Credential-backed post-write authority validation rejects Disabled, Tombstoned, and missing arbitrary canonical user records and deletes each newly written session before it can be returned.

exact.c9.7.passkey-postwrite-epoch.description: Credential-backed post-write authority validation rejects an arbitrary canonical user's stale captured lifecycle epoch and deletes the newly written session.

exact.c9.7.recovery-no-jit.description: A valid-format unconsumed recovery record that names a missing canonical user fails closed through the public recovery endpoint without creating a user or session and without consuming or mutating the recovery material.

exact.c9.11.bootstrap-xor.description: The authenticated Admin create endpoint requires exactly one of temporary password or invitation bootstrap, rejects both and neither, and preserves the password-bootstrap behavior without creating an invitation.

exact.c9.11.crypto-rng.description: The complete invitation issuance core obtains exactly 32 bytes from an injected CryptoRng before persisting the verifier, emitting the structured audit event, and returning the base64url show-once secret; the production wrapper injects OsRng.

exact.c9.11.show-once.description: Admin invitation creation returns a two-part show-once bearer with an exact default 24-hour expiry, leaves the password unconfigured, and authenticated Admin detail cannot retrieve the invitation URL, token, or verifier hash.

exact.c9.11.regeneration.description: Repeated Admin create and regeneration issue a new show-once secret and invalidate every previously returned invitation for the same user.

exact.c9.11.concurrent-consume.description: Two concurrent public acceptance requests for one invitation produce exactly one invite-authenticated session and one rejected replay.

exact.c9.11.lifecycle-fail-closed.description: Expired invitations and invitations whose canonical user becomes Disabled or Tombstoned are rejected without establishing a session.

exact.c9.11.eligibility.description: Configuring a password invalidates the pending invitation, while a federated-only canonical user is ineligible for local invitation bootstrap.
