exact.c9.11.tenant-isolation.description: A tenant-scoped invitation accepted through a different SaaS Host is rejected, while the original tenant Host can consume it.

exact.c9.11.dynamo-verifier-record.description: The production Dynamo invitation adapter persists an exact tenant-scoped field closure containing the verifier hash and invitation metadata but no invitation URL, bearer token, or secret field.

exact.c9.11.dynamo-atomic-consume.description: The production Dynamo invitation adapter sends one transaction that conditionally deletes the exact invitation verifier and writes the tenant-scoped login session with amr=invite.

exact.c9.11.dynamo-issue-reconcile.description: Invitation issuance retries an ambiguous Dynamo transaction with the identical idempotency token and reports success only after a strong read matches the exact active invitation record.

exact.c9.11.dynamo-issue-mismatch.description: After an ambiguous invitation-issuance transaction, strong-read reconciliation rejects a record whose verifier or other exact invitation authority differs from the attempted write.

exact.c9.11.dynamo-accept-reconcile.description: Invitation acceptance retries an ambiguous Dynamo transaction with the identical idempotency token and reports success only after a strong read matches the exact invite-authenticated session.

exact.c9.11.dynamo-accept-mismatch.description: After an ambiguous invitation-acceptance transaction, strong-read reconciliation rejects a session whose invite authentication authority differs from the attempted transaction.

exact.c9.11.web-history.description: The browser removes the invitation bearer from the URL and history before acceptance and redirects a successful invite-authenticated session only to /account.

exact.c9.11.web-retry.description: A failed browser acceptance retains the invitation bearer only in page memory for an explicit retry while the address bar and browser history remain bearer-free.

exact.c9.11.web-show-once.description: The Admin UI sends invitation bootstrap without an initial password and preserves the show-once invitation across copy failure, navigation warnings, and dismissal until the operator explicitly discards it.

exact.c9.11.web-concurrent-regeneration.description: The Admin UI serializes concurrent regeneration gestures into one request and exposes only the resulting replacement invitation.

exact.c9.11.infra.description: The synthesized deployment gives invitations an independent encrypted PITR-enabled TTL table, passes only its table name and configured validity to the auth runtime, and grants the exact Dynamo transaction permissions required for atomic acceptance.

exact.c10.3.kms-adapter.description: The production KMS signer sends Sign with the configured key, RAW message type, and ECDSA_SHA_256, then converts a DER signature containing both required sign padding and a short scalar into the exact 64-byte JOSE r||s form.

exact.c10.3.der-full-width.description: Full-width positive P-256 DER integers become the exact two 32-byte JOSE coordinates without reordering or truncation.

exact.c10.3.der-sign-padding.description: A required DER 0x00 sign byte is removed while the high-bit P-256 scalar remains exactly 32 bytes in JOSE.

exact.c10.3.der-short-padding.description: A short DER scalar is left-padded to its exact 32-byte JOSE coordinate instead of changing its numeric value.

exact.c10.3.jose-roundtrip.description: JOSE to DER and back preserves both 32-byte coordinates, including the DER sign-padding case.

exact.c10.3.malformed-der.description: The DER parser rejects a non-minimal integer with redundant leading zeroes instead of accepting an ambiguous ECDSA encoding.

exact.c10.4.boundary.description: The shared short-lived-item predicate rejects now == expires_at exactly while accepting the preceding second, without applying the token clock-skew allowance.

exact.c10.4.authorization-code.description: POST /token rejects an otherwise valid authorization-code record whose expires_at is in the past even though the record remains physically present in CodeStore.

exact.c10.4.session-token.description: A correct session Bearer can read a physically present authorization-session record, but the read path projects its non-terminal state to expired when expires_at is in the past.

exact.c10.4.session-read-after-await.description: GET /sessions/{id} samples time after the asynchronous authority read and immediately before its authorized response projection, so a non-terminal session reaching expires_at while the read is in flight is returned as expired.

exact.c10.4.jti.description: CIBA rejects an otherwise valid id_token_hint after its still-present JTI authority record is overwritten with an expired expires_at value.

exact.c10.4.jti-read-after-await.description: The shared JTI authority boundary samples time after the asynchronous store read, so a record that reaches expires_at while the read is in flight is classified as expired.

exact.c10.4.grace-read-after-await.description: The refresh grace boundary samples time after the asynchronous cache read, so an entry that reaches expires_at while the read is in flight is not reused.

exact.c10.4.device-token-commit-time.description: The device token path resamples time immediately before its atomic consume, rejects a grant that expires during preceding asynchronous gates as expired_token, and leaves it unconsumed.

exact.c10.4.device-approval-commit-time.description: The device approval path resamples time immediately before its atomic decision, rejects a grant that expires during password-authority lookup, and leaves every grant field unchanged.

exact.c10.4.memory-code-write-fence.description: At now == expires_at, the Memory CodeStore returns NotFound before consumed or lease state, and rejects finalize, lease release, replay marking, and exchange-failure finalization without mutating the still-present authorization-code record.

exact.c10.4.memory-write-fence.description: At now == expires_at, the Memory authorization-session store rejects transition and user binding, while the Memory device store rejects poll claiming, consumption, approval, and consumption rollback without mutating the still-present records.

exact.c10.4.dynamo-code-write-fence.description: The production Dynamo CodeStore binds expires_at > :now into lease acquisition, finalization, lease release, and replay marking; after an acquisition conflict it also classifies an expired consumed row as NotFound before replay state.

exact.c10.4.dynamo-exchange-failure-fenc.description: The production Dynamo exchange-failure transaction binds expires_at > :now into both the authorization-code finalization and authorization-session transition within the same transaction.

exact.c10.4.dynamo-exchange-failure-afte.description: The production Dynamo exchange-failure path resamples time after its strongly consistent authorization-session read, rejects newly expired records, and uses that same commit time for both transaction conditions.

exact.c10.4.dynamo-session-transition-af.description: The production Dynamo authorization-session transition resamples time after each strongly consistent read and uses the refreshed value for both the application expiry decision and the conditional write.

exact.c10.4.dynamo-device-write-fence.description: The production Dynamo device store binds expires_at > :now into the same conditional writes that consume, decide, or roll back consumption of a device grant.

exact.c10.4.dynamo-release-classificatio.description: A Dynamo conditional rejection while releasing an authorization-code lease is classified as the same transient lost-lease outcome as the Memory adapter, rather than a permanent storage failure.

exact.c10.5.persistent-identities.description: The synthesized production stack enables PITR and omits DynamoDB TTL from the Users, Passkey, Clients, and Grants authority tables.

exact.c10.5.unexpired-artifact.description: The shared reclaim decision keeps an otherwise idle client active whenever an unexpired authorization code or session still references it.

exact.c10.5.active-grant.description: At P2, an active Grant is a fail-safe reclaim blocker even when the client is otherwise idle and has no refresh, code, or session reference.

exact.c10.5.idle-tombstone.description: A real reclaim pass converts an idle client with no active references to a tombstone instead of hard deleting the persistent identity immediately.

exact.c10.5.active-refresh.description: A real reclaim pass observes an active refresh family and keeps the owning idle client non-tombstoned.

exact.c10.5.grace-pending.description: A reclaim pass keeps a tombstoned client until the maximum access-token lifetime grace period has elapsed.

exact.c10.5.late-reference.description: Before hard deletion, the reclaim orchestrator rechecks authority and preserves a past-grace tombstone when a late active refresh reference exists.

exact.c10.5.hard-delete.description: A past-grace tombstone with no live authority reference is hard deleted through the reclaim orchestrator.

exact.c10.5.code-reference-atomicity.description: The production Dynamo code adapter writes an authorization code and its client authority reference in one transaction fenced by the active client.

exact.c10.5.refresh-reference-atomicity.description: The production Dynamo refresh adapter writes a family and its active client authority reference in one transaction fenced by the active client.

exact.c10.5.tombstone-revision-fence.description: The production client tombstone conditional update binds the exact authority revision observed before the reclaim decision, closing concurrent issuance races.

exact.c10.5.hard-delete-transaction.description: The production Dynamo client adapter deletes the tenant-scoped client and writes a tenant-scoped durable audit row in one transaction; the audit stays outside the reclaim index and has no expiry field.

exact.c10.5.coverage-required.description: The production authority-reference reader returns a transient fail-closed result after a strongly consistent coverage read when no complete coverage marker exists, without querying references.

exact.c10.5.coverage-version.description: A coverage marker from a different deployment migration version is rejected before any authority-reference absence can be trusted.

exact.c10.5.code-query.description: With exact coverage established, the production code reference lookup performs a strongly consistent bounded Query in the tenant/client partition and excludes codes expiring at the observed instant.

exact.c10.5.refresh-query.description: With exact coverage established, the production refresh reference lookup performs a strongly consistent bounded Query in the same tenant/client authority partition.

exact.c10.5.migration-checkpoints.description: The production authority-reference migration uses bounded strongly consistent pages, persists resumable checkpoints, and publishes code and refresh coverage only with the terminal migration state.

exact.c10.5.migration-generation.description: Migration generation and checkpoint conditions reject stale steps and stale coverage publication after a newer invocation owns the migration state.

exact.c10.6.verify-time-boundaries.description: Real ES256 tokens exercise the production verifier at independent literal boundaries: exp remains valid through +29 seconds and fails at +30, while nbf and iat at +30 pass and +31 fail under the same configured 30-second skew.

exact.c10.7.code-flow.description: After a public authorization code is bound to its registered client, exhausting that authenticated client bucket makes POST /token return 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After; deleting only that bucket lets the identical code and verifier succeed, proving throttling releases the code lease without consuming it.

exact.c10.7.code-release-failure.description: When the authenticated client bucket is exhausted but a transient store failure prevents authorization-code lease release, POST /token returns 503 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After instead of promising ordinary 429 retryability while the lease is still held.

exact.c10.7.code-release-permanent-failu.description: When authorization-code lease release fails permanently after client throttling, POST /token fails closed with 500 server_error and no Retry-After rather than falsely promising a timed retry.

exact.c10.7.code-authenticated-identity.description: With the code-bound client's bucket already exhausted, a confidential authorization-code request whose HTTP Basic client differs from the form client_id is still rejected as invalid_client rather than 429; clearing that authoritative bucket and retrying with the authenticated client succeeds without prior code consumption.

exact.c10.7.refresh.description: After a real code flow creates a refresh family, exhausting the family-bound client bucket makes the refresh request return 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After; the family version remains unchanged and no grace replay entry is created, while deleting only that bucket lets the identical refresh token succeed.

exact.c10.7.refresh-authenticated-identi.description: With the family-bound client's bucket already exhausted, refresh requests with an unknown Basic client or a form client_id conflicting with the authenticated Basic client are still rejected as invalid_client rather than 429; clearing the authoritative bucket lets the same refresh token succeed without prior rotation.

exact.c10.7.workload.description: A valid workload OIDC assertion is mapped to its registered workload client before rate limiting; exhausting that client bucket returns 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After, and deleting only the bucket lets the identical authenticated assertion issue a token.

exact.c10.7.token-exchange.description: A valid RFC 8693 request verifies and maps its workload actor before rate limiting; exhausting the actor client bucket returns 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After, and deleting only the bucket lets the identical subject and actor tokens complete the exchange.

exact.c10.7.tenant-isolation.description: Exhausting one tenant's bucket for a shared client_id leaves the same client_id admitted in a sibling tenant and in the self-hosted partition, proving application-layer keys include the authoritative tenant boundary.

exact.c10.7.device-poll.description: After a real Device Authorization request creates an artifact, exhausting its bound client's aggregate bucket makes POST /token return 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After; last_poll_at remains unset, and clearing only the bucket lets the identical device_code return authorization_pending.

exact.c10.7.ciba-poll.description: After a real CIBA request creates an artifact, exhausting its bound client's aggregate bucket makes POST /token return 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After; last_poll_at remains unset, and clearing only the bucket lets the identical auth_req_id return authorization_pending.

exact.c10.8.global-quota.description: After the tenant-global anonymous registration bucket is exhausted, two distinct source IPs both receive 429 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After and neither request creates a client.

exact.c10.8.global-quota-fail-closed.description: If the mandatory tenant-global anonymous registration quota dependency is absent, POST /register returns 503 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After: 1 and does not create a client.

exact.c10.19.codes.description: Two tenants can hold the same authorization-code value independently: foreign lease acquisition and by-client authority lookup return no record, foreign user cleanup is a no-op, one tenant's finalize state does not consume the sibling record, and deleting one tenant partition leaves the sibling lease intact.

exact.c10.19.clients.description: The same client_id can exist independently in two tenants; a sibling tenant cannot read the first record and each tenant list returns only its own client.

exact.c10.19.users.description: The same email and canonical user_id are isolated across tenant-qualified primary, email, id, and list paths.

exact.c10.19.federated-user.description: A canonical federated user remains invisible to a sibling tenant while its owning tenant can list, disable, tombstone, and permanently fence the identity.

exact.c10.19.grants.description: Grant primary reads and same-user list queries expose only the request tenant even when user identifiers collide across tenants.

exact.c10.19.refresh.description: Refresh-family primary reads, user revocation, and active-client authority checks remain tenant-qualified and cannot observe or revoke a sibling family's state.

exact.c10.19.sessions.description: Session primary reads, user counts, lists, revoke-others, owned deletion, and bulk user revocation remain isolated when the same user_id exists in two tenants.

exact.c10.19.passkeys.description: Passkey user-index listing and bulk deletion affect only the request tenant when canonical user identifiers collide.

exact.c10.19.recovery.description: Recovery lookup and deletion are tenant-qualified, so a sibling tenant cannot read or delete the same logical recovery key.

exact.c10.19.authz-sessions.description: Authorization-session primary reads, client-index lists, and active counts are isolated across named tenants and the legacy flat partition.

exact.c10.19.reclaim.description: Cross-tenant maintenance scans preserve each record's owning tenant, tenant-scoped scans exclude siblings, and tombstone writeback cannot mutate the same client_id in another tenant.

exact.c10.19.magic-links.description: Magic-link consumption and per-email cooldown keys are isolated so one tenant cannot consume another tenant's link or occupy its email cooldown.

exact.c10.19.devices.description: Device-code primary reads, colliding short user_code lookup, and approval state remain isolated between tenants.

exact.c10.19.ciba.description: CIBA request reads, approval, consumption, and user throttle windows remain tenant-qualified even when auth_req_id and user_id collide.

exact.c10.19.workload-trust.description: Colliding workload binding IDs can be created, listed, and deleted independently without overwriting or removing a sibling tenant binding.

exact.c10.19.messages.description: Admin outbox listing exposes only the request tenant's recipient and magic-link body and keeps the legacy flat partition separate.

exact.c10.19.flat-compat.description: Memory ClientStore writes and reads the empty-tenant namespace while a named tenant cannot read the same logical client_id.

exact.c10.19.dynamo-client-read.description: Production Dynamo ClientStore strongly consistent reads serialize the same logical client_id into distinct tenant-qualified primary keys.

exact.c10.19.dynamo-code-keys.description: The production Dynamo authorization-code transaction serializes the same logical code and client into distinct tenant-qualified code primary keys, client values, authority-reference partitions, source identifiers, and client authority-touch keys.

exact.c10.19.dynamo-session-read.description: Production Dynamo SessionStore strongly consistent reads serialize the same logical session_id into distinct tenant-qualified primary keys.

exact.c10.19.dynamo-refresh-read.description: Production Dynamo RefreshStore strongly consistent reads serialize the same logical family_id into distinct tenant-qualified primary keys.

exact.c10.19.saas-http-flow.description: A Host-derived t1 authorization code is invalid_grant on t2 without being consumed, succeeds on t1, and leaves the registered client, issued Grant, and active refresh-family authority visible only in t1.

exact.c10.22a.guard.description: The claims-tier issuer guard accepts a token issuer derived from the request tenant Host, rejects a sibling tenant issuer with HostMismatch, and rejects the SaaS control-plane Host before signing.

exact.c10.22a.counterexample.description: The explicit shared-key counterexample proves that directly trusting a tenant-supplied issuer would let t1 retain t2's issuer, while the production guard rejects that same cross-tenant issuer.

exact.c10.22a.runtime-denial.description: The production HTTP tenant helper rejects t1 attempting to use t2's issuer and records a t1 tenant-boundary denied security event whose subject is the denied t2 issuer.

exact.c10.22a.shared-signer-denial.description: A SaaS claims-tier fixture resolves t1 and t2 to the same signing key, then proves the production tenant-guarded access-token, ID-token, delegation-token, and grant-ref signers each reject a t1 request carrying t2's issuer without incrementing the ES256 sign counter. Private raw-signer counterexamples cryptographically sign all four foreign-issuer artifacts with that same key, proving the application guard is the effective boundary.

exact.c10.22a.issuance-wiring.description: A parsed Rust call-site inventory pins the known SaaS issuer-bearing OAuth issuance families to tenant-guarded signers: authorization code, refresh, token exchange, service/managed workload, device, CIBA, EMA, and grant-ref. It also pins each guarded helper to call issuer_belongs_to_request_tenant before its private raw signer. This target proves source wiring, not control-flow dominance; functional no-sign behavior is proven separately by the shared-signer denial target. SelfHosted X.509 uses its configured issuer through the dedicated mTLS Host exception and remains outside the SaaS claims-tier scope.

exact.c10.21.cookie-session-isolation.description: A P1 SaaS magic-link flow emits nonce and session cookies with the complete __Host- contract and no Domain; the t1 cookie reaches consent on t1, returns to login when manually replayed on t2, and remains valid on t1 after the cross-tenant attempt.

exact.c10.23.user-navigation.description: The Admin users tab restores its tab and server-side query from a bookmarked URL, preserves the filtered view across a full reload, and follows browser back and forward navigation between that view and overview.

exact.c10.23.invalid-tab.description: A bookmarked Admin URL with an unrecognized tab selects the overview tab instead of rendering an invalid view.

exact.c10.23.client-search.description: The Admin clients tab restores a bookmarked client query across reload and browser history, then filters the complete API response independently by client_id, redirect URI, and resource identifier.

exact.c10.23.user-search-pagination.description: The authenticated GET /admin/users endpoint returns a limit=1 page and continuation cursor, accepts that cursor, rejects a malformed cursor, and still finds users outside the unfiltered first page by either case-insensitive email or a distinct canonical user_id.

exact.c10.23.user-search-pagination-dyna.description: The published Dynamo users adapter skips a query-matching foreign-tenant first page, continues Scan pagination, independently finds a later in-tenant user by case-insensitive email or distinct canonical user_id, round-trips the returned cursor into the physical continuation key, rejects a malformed cursor, and issues strongly consistent limit=1 requests.

exact.c10.24.user-memory-monotonic.description: The Memory users adapter advances last_login_at only for an existing active user, preserves the newer timestamp against an older observation, independently updates the same logical user id in two tenants, and leaves the other tenant unchanged.

exact.c10.24.user-dynamo-contract.description: The published Dynamo users adapter captures its real UpdateItem request and proves the tenant-prefixed physical user key, existing-row active-user guard, strictly-monotonic last_login_at condition, and exact observed timestamp.

exact.c10.24.client-memory-daily.description: The Memory client adapter records one tenant-scoped UTC day bucket, leaves same-day activity unchanged, advances on a later day, and never creates a missing client.

exact.c10.24.client-dynamo-contract.description: The published Dynamo client adapter captures its real UpdateItem request and proves the tenant-prefixed physical client key, existing-row guard, strictly-increasing last_used_day condition, and exact UTC day bucket.

exact.c10.24.user-observation-failure.description: A real magic-link callback with an injected users-store activity failure still redirects with a session cookie, while authenticated Admin detail shows the prior last_login_at unchanged.

exact.c10.24.client-observation-failure.description: A real authorization-code exchange with an injected client-store activity failure still returns HTTP 200 and a non-empty access token.

exact.c10.24.password-login.description: A correct temporary password returns change-required without a session; reusing it or supplying a policy-invalid replacement is rejected without changing version 1 or must-change. Only a distinct compliant replacement creates an amr=pwd session, clears must-change through version CAS, records last_login_at, invalidates the temporary password, and permits the replacement password.

exact.c10.24.invitation-login.description: Successful invitation acceptance establishes an invite-authenticated session and records the exact session auth_time as last_login_at; replay is rejected and leaves that timestamp unchanged.

exact.c10.24.passkey-login.description: The public magic-link flow establishes the missing-ACR baseline representation with email AMR, which exact.c12.4.local-class-mapping classifies as canonical baseline; a complete passkey register and verified WebAuthn authenticate flow then establishes a canonical strong session with webauthn and hwk AMR and advances last_login_at.

exact.c10.24.passkey-authority-rollback.description: A valid passkey assertion that loses the credential-authority race is rejected without a session and leaves last_login_at empty.

exact.c10.24.federation-login.description: A verified upstream federation callback creates the canonical federated user and an AS session, then records a non-null last_login_at.

exact.c10.24.federation-disabled-denial.description: A cryptographically verified federation callback for a disabled canonical user is rejected without a cookie or stored session and leaves last_login_at empty.

exact.c10.24.recovery-login.description: Successful recovery establishes a new fenced session and advances last_login_at beyond the prior magic-link login timestamp.

exact.c10.24.recovery-authority-rollback.description: Recovery that loses the password-authority race is rejected without a session and preserves the prior last_login_at.

exact.c10.24.recovery-replay.description: A committed recovery result may replay only the original session for the original operation and code, without advancing last_login_at again; mismatched operations or codes are rejected.

exact.c10.24.token-issuance.description: An unknown authorization code fails without recording activity, while a successful code exchange advances last_used_day; the signal is conservative and does not claim downstream resource-server use or guaranteed token delivery.

exact.c10.24.ciba-push-success.description: A CIBA push client remains unused after request creation; successful minting and delivery advances last_used_day, consumes the request once, and rejects later poll replay.

exact.c10.24.ciba-push-delivery-failure.description: A CIBA push client remains unused before approval; a delivery failure after token minting remains terminal and advances last_used_day because issuance already succeeded.

exact.c10.24.ciba-push-tombstone.description: A client tombstoned between CIBA request and approval is rejected before consumption, Grant creation, token delivery, or last_used_day advancement.

exact.c10.24.admin-user-null.description: Authenticated Admin user list and detail GET responses both return last_login_at as JSON null for a newly provisioned user that has never established an authentication session.

exact.c10.24.admin-client-time.description: Authenticated Admin client list and detail responses convert a stored UTC day bucket into Unix-second last_used_at, return JSON null for a never-used client, and never leak credentials.

exact.c10.24.web-users.description: The Admin users table renders a UTC last-login timestamp and the localized never-logged-in state from non-null and null API values.

exact.c10.24.web-clients.description: The Admin clients table renders a UTC day for observed token issuance and the localized never-used state for a null activity value.

exact.c10.25.api-defaults.description: The authenticated Admin users endpoint hides tombstoned users by default, treats explicit non_deleted identically, returns exact active, disabled, tombstoned, and all views, and rejects an unknown status.

exact.c10.25.api-search-pagination.description: The Admin users endpoint composes lifecycle status with search, skips a leading tombstone before filling the requested page size, and returns a continuation cursor only while matching users remain.

exact.c10.25.dynamo-scan-pages.description: The Dynamo users adapter continues across tombstoned and foreign-tenant physical scan pages until it fills the requested tenant-scoped non-deleted page.

exact.c10.25.dynamo-tail-cursor.description: The Dynamo users adapter emits a cursor when a full logical page leaves unconsumed matching items in the final physical scan response, then returns those items exactly once.

exact.c10.25.dynamo-filtered-tail.description: After filling a logical page, the Dynamo users adapter scans a tail containing only filtered records to exhaustion and does not advertise an empty continuation page.

exact.c10.25.web-status.description: The Admin users UI hides deleted users by default and persists explicit lifecycle filters through URL state, reload, and browser history.

exact.c10.25.web-load-more.description: Loading another Admin users page retains the selected lifecycle filter in both the request and URL state.

exact.c10.25.web-delete.description: Deleting a user removes the tombstoned record from the default non-deleted Admin users view.

exact.c10.25.web-stale-response.description: A delayed response for an earlier lifecycle filter cannot overwrite the Admin users view selected by the current URL.

exact.c10.25.web-mutation-latest.description: When a pending user mutation completes, the Admin users UI reloads the latest lifecycle filter instead of an obsolete request snapshot.

exact.c11.1.regional-id.description: The regional runtime issues the literal r1_<region>_<activation-revision>_<opaque> frame and accepts only non-empty identifiers owned by the exact currently admitted Region and revision.

exact.c11.3.quiescence-fence.description: A target Region configured to activate 330 seconds in the future remains inactive before the persisted activation_not_before boundary, including one second before it, and becomes active only at the exact boundary.

exact.c11.4.mrk-create.description: The production KMS adapter sends CreateKey for both EC P-256 and RSA-2048 with MultiRegion=true, SIGN_VERIFY usage, and the full tenant generation tag set.

exact.c11.4.regional-probes.description: For both EC and RSA generations, the production KMS adapter reads and signs with the primary and every configured replica Region ARN, uses the fixed readiness challenge and exact algorithm, verifies each signature locally, and accepts only identical public key identity. A real AlreadyExistsException replay proves retries still continue into replica-local probes.

exact.c11.4.probe-fail-closed.description: For both EC and RSA, the production readiness path rejects a validly encoded signature made by the wrong key and rejects a replica whose locally verified public key differs from the primary, so neither a no-op verifier nor divergent regional material can pass.

exact.c11.4.snapshot-gate.description: During initial onboarding, primary and replica readiness failures retain the generation in Provisioning with no served or ready snapshot, and expiry transitions to Failed with cleanup while still serving nothing. During rotation, the same replica-readiness failure keeps the previous generation unchanged and ready while the new candidate remains unpublished.

exact.c11.4.regional-runtime.description: A serving runtime in another configured Region rewrites both EC and RSA multi-Region key ARNs to that local Region before constructing its signer, retaining the shared MRK key identity.

exact.c11.4.single-region-fail-closed.description: A legacy single-Region EC/RSA snapshot is accepted only in its origin Region and is rejected as permanently unavailable when a runtime in another Region attempts to serve it.

exact.c11.1.failback-revision.description: A primary-to-standby-to-primary sequence advances the activation revision every time; failback rejects both the first primary artifact and the standby artifact while accepting only the newly issued primary artifact.

exact.c11.1.code-refresh-owner.description: The public token endpoint issues an authorization code and refresh family under one activation, returns 503 region_inactive without tokens for both handles while the next revision is inside its persisted 330-second quiescence fence, then rejects both old handles after activation and accepts only a newly authorized code.

exact.c11.1.jti-owner.description: A real signed access token and its Region-local JTI mapping are created under revision one; the public token-exchange path returns 503 region_inactive without a token while revision two is inside its persisted 330-second quiescence fence, then revision three rejects the otherwise valid old subject token before consulting its stale JTI authority.

exact.c11.1.dynamo-admission.description: The production Dynamo adapter sends one TransactGetItems request for the exact control, Region, and fence keys. A split-brain snapshot returns public 503 temporarily_unavailable, while missing rows return public 503 region_inactive; neither response advertises an active Region.

exact.c11.1.split-brain.description: The coordinated snapshot parser rejects an active Region row when the coordinator names another Region, remains quiescing, or carries a different revision.

exact.c11.1.persistent-fence.description: The production Region snapshot parser rejects active-bit, activation-time, and revision drift between the Region row and its persistent fence, preventing a cold start from reviving an older writer.

exact.c11.1.primary-topology.description: The primary CDK template replicates all 16 durable authority tables plus the retained activation fence to the reviewed standby Region and gives none of the replay/runtime tables a replica.

exact.c11.1.runtime-fence-iam.description: The synthesized primary passes Region control to every serving and authority-writing runtime, grants the exact TransactGetItems permission, and keeps Admin runtime state in the Region-local table.

exact.c11.1.standby-topology.description: The standby CDK template imports every replicated authority table, creates all 20 Region-local tables including the migration reference table, and wires the serving runtime to local replay state and replica-local bootstrap configuration.

exact.c11.1.edge-affinity.description: The executable drill recognizes the current 16-table authority and 20-table Region-local inventories, waits through quiescence, admits exactly one coordinated writer before switching CloudFront, and purges all standby-local state before failback.

exact.c11.1.governance-drill-topology.description: The governance live drill accepts the same complete 20-table standby Region-local inventory, including the authority-reference migration table, so current deployments are not rejected by a stale operational gate.

exact.c11.2.refresh-grant-gate.description: The public refresh flow rejects a revoked authoritative Grant while the Region-local refresh family remains active and version zero, proving the Grant status gate runs before regional refresh consumption; a legacy family without a Grant remains compatible.

exact.c11.2.dynamo-grant-read.description: The production Dynamo Grant adapter sends a strongly consistent GetItem for the tenant-prefixed Grant authority key and returns the revoked authority status consumed by the refresh gate.

exact.c10.9.consent-csrf.description: The real authorize-to-consent continuation preserves state and issues distinct CSRF tokens bound to both the browser session and authorize request; missing, tampered, cross-request, and cross-session tokens are rejected, and a browser-invented query without an authorization-session pointer cannot issue a code.

exact.c10.9.authz-session-required.description: If the AS cannot persist the authorization session, the public authorize endpoint returns 503 instead of continuing with an empty session pointer.

exact.c10.9b.cloudfront-wiring.description: The synthesized CloudFront distribution gives both /login and /consent explicit SPA behaviors that reference the same ResponseHeadersPolicy whose CSP overrides with frame-ancestors 'none' and whose X-Frame-Options override is DENY.

exact.c10.10.cors-partition.description: One HTTP matrix fixes all five CORS classes: public GET and protocol/open-registration preflights use wildcard origin without credentials, while cookie-bearing session, management, and browser-navigation endpoints emit no CORS credentials or origin.

exact.c10.10.router-partition.description: A structural guard pins every route module to the wildcard no-cookie or same-origin group and forbids credentials in the centralized wildcard CorsLayer.

exact.c10.11a.rotation-overlap-jwks.description: A tenant key rotation moves from publish-ahead with the old EC/RSA generation active to active overlap with the new generation active. In both phases the public /jwks.json endpoint returns the same complete two-generation EC+RSA key set; each response kid is independently recomputed from the literal RFC 7638 canonical JSON and SHA-256, and ES256 access-shaped JWS, RS256 ID-shaped JWS, and production SSF SET values signed by both generations verify only with the corresponding key selected by kid. Retirement is rejected one second early; at the deadline public JWKS retains only the new pair, new values still verify, and all old values fail against every remaining key.

exact.c10.11b.rotation-windows.description: The production tenant-key orchestrator freezes publish-ahead at no less than the public JWKS max-age, rejects activation one second early, and switches exactly at the boundary. It derives retirement from the maximum access-token, ID-token, and immutable SSF SET retry lifetimes plus clock skew, keeps both EC/RSA generations published with no deletion one second before that deadline, and retires only the old pair exactly at the deadline.

exact.c10.12.public-jwks.description: A tenant-managed rotation in publish-ahead state takes the production zero-overlap emergency transition immediately, without activation or retirement deadlines. The public /jwks.json endpoint then exposes only the new EC and RSA pair; new ES256 access-shaped JWS, RS256 ID-shaped JWS, and production SSF SET values verify, while all three old-generation values fail against every remaining key.

exact.c10.12.provisioner.description: The production tenant-key command processor accepts emergency_revoke one second after publish-ahead, atomically commits the complete new EC/RSA generation with no graceful publish-ahead or artifact-lifetime wait, schedules both old KMS keys for deletion, records a backward-compatible durable emergency operation marker, and handles an identical retry without repeating deletion.

exact.c10.12.runbook.description: The executable KMS drill has an explicit emergency-only branch before the graceful-retirement gate. It switches Auth and SSF to new-key-only publication without the retirement sleep, requires CloudFront /jwks.json invalidation, waits for that invalidation to complete, rejects the old token, and records emergency_revoke in the canonical rotation audit.

exact.c10.13.control-plane.description: The synthesized SaaS deployment provisions the durable tenant-key registry, command queue, and tenant-key provisioner for the configured tenant set. The provisioner receives the exact replica Region list and owns ReplicateKey plus replica GetPublicKey and Sign permissions, while Auth and SSF runtimes receive TENANT_KEYS_TABLE but no shared SIGNING_KEY_ID or RSA_SIGNING_KEY_ID fallback.

exact.c10.13.complete-pairs.description: The public SaaS JWKS seam rejects unknown tenants and every empty, partially provisioned, or failed tenant key record. Two ready tenants independently expose exactly one EC and one RSA key, and their complete kid sets are disjoint.

exact.c10.13.es256-forgery.description: An ES256 access token signed by tenant A is rejected against tenant B's EC JWKS both when it carries A's natural kid (UnknownKid) and when it forges B's kid while retaining A's signature (BadSignature).

exact.c10.13.rs256-forgery.description: An RS256 ID token signed by tenant A is rejected against tenant B's RSA JWKS both when it carries A's natural kid (UnknownKid) and when it forges B's kid while retaining A's signature (BadSignature).

exact.c10.16.cloudfront-ttl.description: The synthesized CloudFront distribution gives /jwks.json an explicit API-origin behavior whose cache policy fixes min/default/max TTL at 300 seconds, partitions entries by the forwarded tenant host, excludes cookies and query strings, preserves origin authentication, and forwards only standard CORS request headers.

exact.c10.17.hot-path-zero-cedar.description: AST call inspection proves the token, token-exchange, and refresh sources do not directly call Cedar evaluation or background recomputation; token-exchange and refresh must call policy_freshness::stale_gate, whose actual calls exclude evaluation, policy application, and recomputation.

exact.c10.17.cold-path-cedar.description: AST call inspection and direct runtime assertions prove the Grant-creation and background-recompute cold paths each read the active policy artifact exactly once and apply the policy-specific narrowing from {read,write} to {read}, preventing the hot-path absence guard from passing because authorization was disconnected entirely.

exact.c10.17.refresh-stale-read-gate.description: A real refresh-token request with a stale Grant returns 503 temporarily_unavailable with a positive Retry-After and no access token, leaves the refresh family unrotated, and performs zero ES256 signing attempts. A real recompute pass advances the Grant; with a policy-artifact read failure then armed, the same refresh token succeeds and rotates once without reading the artifact, increments the signing counter, and leaves the failure pending for an explicit cold read.

exact.c10.17.publish-activate.description: The cold publish path writes the policy artifact before activating policy version 1, after which policy application reads the artifact and narrows the Grant.

exact.c10.17.publish-idempotent.description: Publishing identical policy text is idempotent and does not bump the active version, while changed policy text activates the next version.

exact.c10.17.publish-failure.description: Invalid Cedar text and an injected policy-artifact write failure both fail publication without activating or advancing the current policy version; the failed artifact write leaves no version-1 artifact.

exact.c10.17.recompute-narrow.description: Background recomputation narrows a stale Grant's effective scopes, advances effective_pv to the current policy version, and preserves the original authorization ceiling.

exact.c10.17.recompute-reloosen.description: After policy relaxation to read, write, and policy-only delete, background recomputation restores only the consented read/write scopes from the preserved authorized set and does not expand the authoritative consent record.

exact.c10.17.recompute-revoke.description: Background recomputation revokes a resource-bearing Grant when the new policy denies every evaluable permission and emits the corresponding security event.

exact.c10.17.recompute-dry-run.description: Dry-run recomputation reports only the stale Grant scan and leaves the complete authoritative Grant snapshot unchanged.

exact.c10.17.recompute-cas.description: Grant recomputation writes are revision fenced: stale revisions, missing Grants, and already revoked Grants cannot be overwritten or revived, and a real recompute pass cannot overwrite a concurrent revision bump or stamp the old snapshot complete.

exact.c10.17.recompute-revoke-fence.description: A stale recompute snapshot cannot revoke a concurrently updated Grant: a real recompute pass observes the injected revision conflict, reports it, and leaves the authoritative Grant active and unstamped; a revoke using the current revision still succeeds.

exact.c10.17.resource-less-preserve.description: A resource-less Grant has no evaluable unit, so background recomputation preserves it, records the current policy version, and does not revoke it under a deny-all policy.

exact.c10.17.empty-scope-preserve.description: A resource with no scopes and no authorization details has no evaluable unit, so background recomputation preserves the active Grant and changes only the effective policy-version completion stamp and revision.

exact.c3.1.rotation-and-opaque-handle.description: A real refresh handle contains a 24-byte opaque family reference rather than user or client claims; an unknown server-side family fails without recording activity, while a valid rotation advances last_used_day and returns a distinct next version with an ES256 at+jwt access token.

exact.c3.1.concurrent-atomic-rotation.description: With grace disabled, concurrent consumption of one current refresh version has exactly one winner; replay then revokes the whole family, including the winner's new handle.

exact.c3.1.dynamo-conditional-cas.description: The production Dynamo refresh adapter conditionally acquires an expiring owner-fenced signing lease, strongly classifies conflicts, rejects stale-owner release, and finalizes the family version plus encrypted grace row in one two-item transaction guarded by the exact owner, expected version, non-revoked state, and unexpired lease.

exact.c3.1.reuse-revokes-family.description: Reusing a rotated refresh handle with grace disabled rejects the old value and revokes the whole family, including the current value.

exact.c3.2.same-request-cache.description: A byte-equivalent retry of a rotated refresh handle inside the grace window returns the same cached access and refresh tokens, and the family remains usable.

exact.c3.2.request-fingerprint-mismatch.description: Changing scope from omitted to the explicit full authorized set, or changing to another authorized resource, while replaying a rotated refresh handle is treated as reuse, returns no token, and revokes the rotated family.

exact.c3.2.single-decode.description: Distinct wire scope values that parse to the single literal scope a%20b versus the two scopes a and b remain distinct after the HTTP form boundary, so replay is treated as reuse and revokes the rotated family.

exact.c3.2.origin-pkce-binding.description: A PKCE code exchange persists the verified originating challenge in the refresh family, and authority drift before an old-token replay changes the grace fingerprint, returns no token, and revokes the rotated family.

exact.c3.2.client-identity-mismatch.description: A different registered public client identity is rejected without state change for the current refresh version, then receives no token and revokes the original client's family when replaying the rotated old version.

exact.c3.2.dpop-identity-mismatch.description: A current-version wrong DPoP key is rejected without state change, a same-key retry returns the exact cached tokens, and a different key replaying the rotated old handle receives no token and revokes the family.

exact.c3.2.cleanup-failure-retry.description: Injected transient and permanent refresh-revoke and grace-delete failures return token-free fail-closed errors instead of falsely reporting revocation; the selector proves both mutations are independently attempted, a revoke failure leaves the current refresh usable, and a delete failure leaves the family revoked before cleanup succeeds on the next request.

exact.c3.4.envelope-roundtrip.description: The real Dynamo GraceStore adapter requests an AES-256 data key with the exact family/version encryption context, stores the token response only inside the ciphertext envelope while retaining only key/matching/TTL metadata in plaintext, round-trips the complete cached response through KMS Decrypt, and rejects ciphertext moved to another family or version because the GCM AAD no longer matches.

exact.c3.4.delete-only-runtime.description: A DynamoGraceStore constructed without the envelope key rejects real put/get operations before any AWS request while retaining Dynamo family cleanup without KMS access.

exact.c3.4.token-route-scope.description: The token runtime route scope exposes POST /token while returning 404 for discovery and Admin surfaces.

exact.c3.4.non-token-route-scope.description: The non-token runtime route scope returns 404 for POST /token while continuing to serve discovery.

exact.c3.4.primary-runtime-isolation.description: The primary CDK template gives only TokenFn GenerateDataKey/Decrypt and full GraceTable access, limits NonTokenFn to Query/Delete without the grace key, and binds POST/OPTIONS /token exclusively to TokenFn.

exact.c3.4.standby-runtime-isolation.description: The standby CDK template preserves the same TokenFn-only grace-key authority, NonTokenFn delete-only table boundary, and exact POST/OPTIONS /token route split.

exact.c3.3.public-bearer-window.description: A public client without DPoP receives the cached response inside the observed at-most-five-second grace window; replay after expiry is rejected and revokes the rotated family.

exact.c10.1.code-auth-failure.description: A wrong confidential-client secret presented after code lease acquisition returns an authentication challenge, releases the lease without consuming the code, and permits the correctly authenticated client to exchange the same code.

exact.c10.1.code-kms-transient.description: A transient access-token signer failure on the public authorization-code /token path returns 503 with a positive Retry-After and no token fields, then the same code succeeds on retry because its lease was released rather than consumed.

exact.c10.1.code-finalize-failure.description: After signing succeeds, an injected authorization-code finalize failure returns no token, leaves the signing lease in place so an immediate retry cannot sign again, and allows the still-unconsumed code to be reclaimed and exchanged after lease expiry.

exact.c10.1.code-owner-fence-memory.description: After an authorization-code lease expires and a new owner acquires it, the stale owner can neither finalize the code nor release the replacement lease; only the current owner can finalize.

exact.c10.1.refresh-kms-transient.description: A transient signer failure on refresh returns 503 with Retry-After and no token fields, leaves the family version unchanged, releases the signing lease, and lets the same refresh handle retry to the next version.

exact.c10.1.refresh-finalize-failure.description: An injected refresh finalize failure after signing returns no token, advances neither family version nor grace state, keeps the unexpired owner lease so an immediate retry cannot invoke the signer again, and lets the unchanged refresh handle rotate successfully after expiry reclaim.

exact.c10.1.refresh-owner-fence-memory.description: The Memory refresh adapter returns a positive lock delay, permits expiry reclaim, rejects stale-owner finalize and release, and atomically advances the current version while publishing the matching grace response for the current owner.

exact.c10.2.client-credentials-kms.description: A transient signer failure on workload client_credentials returns 503 with Retry-After and no access, refresh, ID, or token-type fields.

exact.c10.2.token-exchange-kms.description: A transient signer failure on RFC 8693 token exchange returns 503 with Retry-After and no access, refresh, ID, or token-type fields.

exact.c10.2.device-kms.description: A transient signer failure on an approved device-code poll returns 503 with Retry-After and no tokens, rolls consumed back to false, and permits issuance after the advertised polling backoff.

exact.c10.2.ciba-kms.description: A transient signer failure on an approved CIBA poll returns 503 with Retry-After and no tokens, rolls consumed back to false, and permits issuance after the advertised polling backoff.

exact.c10.2.ema-kms.description: A transient signer failure on the EMA JWT-bearer grant returns no-store 503 with Retry-After and no token; the already committed assertion replay fence remains consumed rather than allowing duplicate assertion use.

exact.c10.2.proactive-gate.description: The production proactive KMS gate consumes the configured sign permit, then sheds the next request with 503, Retry-After, and temporarily_unavailable before another signing budget is spent.

exact.c10.2.test-run-isolation.description: The deterministic live-test run identifier selects a dedicated global-kms-sign:test bucket while normal runtime retains the shared production bucket.

exact.c10.2.test-run-validation.description: The proactive-gate harness accepts only an exact 128-bit lowercase hexadecimal run identifier and rejects missing, short, long, uppercase, and non-hex identifiers.

exact.c10.2.gate-placement.description: A source-structure guard enumerates authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, token-exchange, device_code, CIBA, and EMA JWT-bearer production signing calls and requires both the tenant and global proactive KMS gates in the same async function before each call.
